
Act as Senior java developer,I want to build below project. First read complete requirement. Don't start implementing yet. 1. Business Scenario
"ArtiCurated," a boutique online marketplace, sells high-value artisanal goods. Their business is growing, and they need a reliable system to manage the entire lifecycle of an order, from payment to potential return and refund. Because their products are unique, their returns process has several manual approval steps and requires clear tracking.
2. Core Functional Requirements
   You are tasked with building the backend for their order management system. It should be a single, well-structured application
   2.1. Complex Order State Management An Order must progress through a defined lifecycle. You must implement a state machine to manage this, enforcing the correct transitions. The states are:
   · PENDING_PAYMENT -> PAID -> PROCESSING_IN_WAREHOUSE -> SHIPPED -> DELIVERED
   · An order can also be CANCELLED from PENDING_PAYMENT or PAID (if not yet processed).
   2.2. Multi-Step Returns Workflow A Return request also has its own lifecycle and must be implemented as a state machine.
   · A return can only be initiated for an order that is in the DELIVERED state.
   · The states for a Return are:
   o REQUESTED: The customer initiates the return.
   o APPROVED / REJECTED: A store manager reviews the request and approves or rejects it.
   o IN_TRANSIT: The customer has shipped the item back.
   o RECEIVED: The warehouse confirms receipt of the returned item.
   o COMPLETED: The refund is successfully processed.
   · The system must log the history of all state changes for both orders and returns for auditing purposes.
   2.3. Asynchronous Background Jobs Certain actions should not block the user or the main application thread. These must be implemented using a background job processing library (e.g., Hangfire, Celery, Sidekiq, or a simple custom solution) or decoupled through Message queues (e.g. RabbitMQ, Apache ActiveMQ, AWS SQS, etc…)
   · PDF Invoice Generation: When an order transitions to SHIPPED, a background job should be queued to generate a PDF invoice (you can use a library to create a simple dummy PDF) and simulate emailing it.
   · Refund Processing: When a return's status becomes COMPLETED, a background job must be queued to make an API call to a mock payment gateway service to process the refund.

# ArtiCurated Order Management System Implementation

## Project Overview

This is a complete Spring Boot application implementing a state machine-driven order management system with asynchronous processing capabilities for a boutique online marketplace.

| Database          | PostgreSQL + Spring Data JPA     | Flyway migrations                           |
| State Machine     | Spring State Machine             | Configured via OrderStateMachineConfig.java |
| Background Jobs   | RabbitMQ + Spring AMQP           | RabbitTemplate, @RabbitListener             |
| API Documentation | OpenAPI 3.0 (Swagger)            | Auto-generated from controllers             |
| Testing           | JUnit 5, Mockito, Testcontainers | Postgres + RabbitMQ containers              |
| Containerization  | Docker & Docker Compose          | Multi-service integration tests             |

### 4. State Machine Configuration

```java
// statemachine/OrderStateMachineConfig.java
@Configuration
@EnableStateMachine
public class OrderStateMachineConfig extends StateMachineConfigurerAdapter<OrderState, OrderEvent> {
    
    @Override
    public void configure(StateMachineStateConfigurer<OrderState, OrderEvent> states) throws Exception {
        states
            .withStates()
            .initial(OrderState.PENDING_PAYMENT)
            .states(EnumSet.allOf(OrderState.class));
    }
    
    @Override
    public void configure(StateMachineTransitionConfigurer<OrderState, OrderEvent> transitions) throws Exception {
        transitions
            .withExternal()
                .source(OrderState.PENDING_PAYMENT).target(OrderState.PAID)
                .event(OrderEvent.PAYMENT_RECEIVED)
            .and()
            .withExternal()
                .source(OrderState.PAID).target(OrderState.PROCESSING_IN_WAREHOUSE)
                .event(OrderEvent.START_PROCESSING)
            .and()
            .withExternal()
                .source(OrderState.PROCESSING_IN_WAREHOUSE).target(OrderState.SHIPPED)
                .event(OrderEvent.SHIP_ORDER)
                .action(shipOrderAction())
            .and()
            .withExternal()
                .source(OrderState.SHIPPED).target(OrderState.DELIVERED)
                .event(OrderEvent.DELIVER_ORDER)
            .and()
            .withExternal()
                .source(OrderState.PENDING_PAYMENT).target(OrderState.CANCELLED)
                .event(OrderEvent.CANCEL_ORDER)
            .and()
            .withExternal()
                .source(OrderState.PAID).target(OrderState.CANCELLED)
                .event(OrderEvent.CANCEL_ORDER);
    }
    
    @Bean
    public Action<OrderState, OrderEvent> shipOrderAction() {
        return context -> {
            // Trigger invoice generation background job
            Long orderId = (Long) context.getExtendedState().getVariables().get("orderId");
            messageProducer.sendInvoiceGenerationMessage(orderId);
        };
    }
}
```


### 5. Order Service Implementation

```java
// service/impl/OrderServiceImpl.java
@Service
@Transactional
@RequiredArgsConstructor
public class OrderServiceImpl implements OrderService {
    
    private final OrderRepository orderRepository;
    private final OrderStateHistoryRepository stateHistoryRepository;
    private final StateMachine<OrderState, OrderEvent> stateMachine;
    
    @Override
    public Order createOrder(CreateOrderRequest request) {
        Order order = Order.builder()
            .orderNumber(generateOrderNumber())
            .customerEmail(request.getCustomerEmail())
            .totalAmount(request.getTotalAmount())
            .currentState(OrderState.PENDING_PAYMENT)
            .build();
            
        order = orderRepository.save(order);
        recordStateChange(order, null, OrderState.PENDING_PAYMENT, "Order created");
        
        return order;
    }
    
    @Override
    public Order transitionOrderState(Long orderId, OrderEvent event) {
        Order order = orderRepository.findById(orderId)
            .orElseThrow(() -> new EntityNotFoundException("Order not found"));
            
        OrderState previousState = order.getCurrentState();
        
        // Configure and start state machine
        stateMachine.getExtendedState().getVariables().put("orderId", orderId);
        stateMachine.sendEvent(event);
        
        OrderState newState = stateMachine.getState().getId();
        
        if (!previousState.equals(newState)) {
            order.setCurrentState(newState);
            order = orderRepository.save(order);
            recordStateChange(order, previousState, newState, "State transition via " + event);
        }
        
        return order;
    }
    
    private void recordStateChange(Order order, OrderState fromState, OrderState toState, String reason) {
        OrderStateHistory history = OrderStateHistory.builder()
            .order(order)
            .fromState(fromState)
            .toState(toState)
            .reason(reason)
            .changedAt(LocalDateTime.now())
            .build();
            
        stateHistoryRepository.save(history);
    }
}
```


### 6. RabbitMQ Configuration

```java
// config/RabbitMQConfig.java
@Configuration
@EnableRabbit
public class RabbitMQConfig {
    
    public static final String INVOICE_QUEUE = "invoice.generation.queue";
    public static final String REFUND_QUEUE = "refund.processing.queue";
    public static final String EXCHANGE = "articurated.exchange";
    
    @Bean
    public DirectExchange exchange() {
        return new DirectExchange(EXCHANGE);
    }
    
    @Bean
    public Queue invoiceQueue() {
        return QueueBuilder.durable(INVOICE_QUEUE).build();
    }
    
    @Bean
    public Queue refundQueue() {
        return QueueBuilder.durable(REFUND_QUEUE).build();
    }
    
    @Bean
    public Binding invoiceBinding() {
        return BindingBuilder.bind(invoiceQueue()).to(exchange()).with("invoice.generate");
    }
    
    @Bean
    public Binding refundBinding() {
        return BindingBuilder.bind(refundQueue()).to(exchange()).with("refund.process");
    }
}
```


### 7. Message Consumers for Background Jobs

```java
// messaging/InvoiceMessageConsumer.java
@Component
@RequiredArgsConstructor
@Slf4j
public class InvoiceMessageConsumer {
    
    private final InvoiceService invoiceService;
    
    @RabbitListener(queues = RabbitMQConfig.INVOICE_QUEUE)
    public void handleInvoiceGeneration(@Payload Long orderId) {
        log.info("Processing invoice generation for order: {}", orderId);
        
        try {
            invoiceService.generateInvoice(orderId);
            log.info("Invoice generated successfully for order: {}", orderId);
        } catch (Exception e) {
            log.error("Failed to generate invoice for order: {}", orderId, e);
        }
    }
}
```


### 8. REST Controllers

```java
// controller/OrderController.java
@RestController
@RequestMapping("/api/orders")
@RequiredArgsConstructor
@Validated
public class OrderController {
    
    private final OrderService orderService;
    
    @PostMapping
    @ResponseStatus(HttpStatus.CREATED)
    public ResponseEntity<OrderDTO> createOrder(@Valid @RequestBody CreateOrderRequest request) {
        Order order = orderService.createOrder(request);
        return ResponseEntity.ok(OrderDTO.from(order));
    }
    
    @PutMapping("/{orderId}/transition")
    public ResponseEntity<OrderDTO> transitionOrder(
            @PathVariable Long orderId,
            @RequestParam OrderEvent event) {
        Order order = orderService.transitionOrderState(orderId, event);
        return ResponseEntity.ok(OrderDTO.from(order));
    }
    
    @GetMapping("/{orderId}")
    public ResponseEntity<OrderDTO> getOrder(@PathVariable Long orderId) {
        Order order = orderService.getOrderById(orderId);
        return ResponseEntity.ok(OrderDTO.from(order));
    }
    
    @GetMapping("/{orderId}/history")
    public ResponseEntity<List<OrderStateHistoryDTO>> getOrderHistory(@PathVariable Long orderId) {
        List<OrderStateHistory> history = orderService.getOrderHistory(orderId);
        return ResponseEntity.ok(history.stream().map(OrderStateHistoryDTO::from).collect(Collectors.toList()));
    }
}
```

### 3. **Advanced State Machine Implementation**

**Distributed State Machine with Saga Pattern:**

```java
// Saga orchestrator for complex multi-service transactions
@Component
@RequiredArgsConstructor
public class OrderProcessingSaga {
    
    private final PaymentService paymentService;
    private final InventoryService inventoryService;
    private final NotificationService notificationService;
    
    @SagaOrchestrationStart
    public void processOrder(OrderCreatedEvent event) {
        SagaTransaction.builder()
            .step("RESERVE_INVENTORY", () -> inventoryService.reserveItems(event.getOrderId()))
            .step("PROCESS_PAYMENT", () -> paymentService.processPayment(event.getPaymentDetails()))
            .step("SEND_CONFIRMATION", () -> notificationService.sendOrderConfirmation(event.getCustomerEmail()))
            .compensate("RELEASE_INVENTORY", () -> inventoryService.releaseReservation(event.getOrderId()))
            .compensate("REFUND_PAYMENT", () -> paymentService.refundPayment(event.getPaymentId()))
            .execute();
    }
}
```

**Database Sharding Strategy:**

```java
@Configuration
public class DatabaseShardingConfig {
    
    @Bean
    public ShardingSphereDataSource dataSource() {
        return ShardingSphereDataSourceFactory.createDataSource(
            createDataSourceMap(),
            createShardingRuleConfig(),
            new Properties()
        );
    }
    
    private ShardingRuleConfiguration createShardingRuleConfig() {
        ShardingRuleConfiguration config = new ShardingRuleConfiguration();
        
        // Shard orders by customer_id
        config.getTableRuleConfigs().add(createOrderTableRule());
        config.getBindingTableGroups().add("orders, order_items");
        
        return config;
    }
    
    private ShardingTableRuleConfiguration createOrderTableRule() {
        return ShardingTableRuleConfiguration.builder()
            .logicTable("orders")
            .actualDataNodes("ds${0..2}.orders_${0..9}")
            .databaseShardingStrategy(new StandardShardingStrategyConfiguration("customer_id", "databaseShardingAlgorithm"))
            .tableShardingStrategy(new StandardShardingStrategyConfiguration("order_id", "tableShardingAlgorithm"))
            .build();
    }
}
```

```yaml
# kafka-config.yml
kafka:
  topics:
    order-events:

    return-events:
      partitions: 6

      retention: 168h
```

**Event Sourcing Implementation:**

```java
@Component
public class OrderEventStore {
    
    @Autowired
    private KafkaTemplate<String, OrderEvent> kafkaTemplate;
    
    public void saveEvent(OrderEvent event) {
        String partitionKey = event.getOrderId().toString();
        kafkaTemplate.send("order-events", partitionKey, event);
    }
    
    @KafkaListener(topics = "order-events", groupId = "order-projection-group")
    public void handleOrderEvent(OrderEvent event) {
        switch (event.getType()) {
            case ORDER_CREATED -> updateOrderProjection(event);
            case ORDER_PAID -> triggerInventoryReservation(event);
            case ORDER_SHIPPED -> generateInvoiceAsync(event);
            case ORDER_DELIVERED -> enableReturnOption(event);
        }
    }
}
```

```java
@Configuration
@EnableCaching
public class CacheConfiguration {
    
    // L1 Cache: Application-level (Caffeine)
    @Bean
    @Primary
    public CacheManager caffeineCacheManager() {
        CaffeineCacheManager manager = new CaffeineCacheManager();
        manager.setCaffeine(Caffeine.newBuilder()
            .maximumSize(10_000)
            .expireAfterWrite(5, TimeUnit.MINUTES)
            .recordStats());
        return manager;
    }
    
    // L2 Cache: Distributed (Redis)
    @Bean
    public CacheManager redisCacheManager(LettuceConnectionFactory connectionFactory) {
        RedisCacheConfiguration config = RedisCacheConfiguration.defaultCacheConfig()
            .entryTtl(Duration.ofMinutes(30))
            .serializeKeysWith(RedisSerializationContext.SerializationPair.fromSerializer(new StringRedisSerializer()))
            .serializeValuesWith(RedisSerializationContext.SerializationPair.fromSerializer(new GenericJackson2JsonRedisSerializer()));
            
        return RedisCacheManager.builder(connectionFactory)
            .cacheDefaults(config)
            .build();
    }
}
```

### 8. **API Gateway with Rate Limiting and Circuit Breaker**

```java
// gateway-service implementation
@Component
public class OrderGatewayFilter implements GlobalFilter {
    
    private final CircuitBreakerFactory circuitBreakerFactory;
    private final RateLimiter rateLimiter;
    
    @Override
    public Mono<Void> filter(ServerWebExchange exchange, GatewayFilterChain chain) {
        String customerId = extractCustomerId(exchange.getRequest());
        
        return rateLimiter.isAllowed("customer:" + customerId, 100) // 100 requests per minute
            .flatMap(allowed -> {
                if (!allowed.isAllowed()) {
                    exchange.getResponse().setStatusCode(HttpStatus.TOO_MANY_REQUESTS);
                    return exchange.getResponse().setComplete();
                }
                
                return circuitBreakerFactory
                    .create("order-service")
                    .run(() -> chain.filter(exchange), throwable -> handleFallback(exchange));
            });
    }
}
```

## **Scalability Benefits of This Architecture:**

### **Horizontal Scaling**

- **Stateless microservices** can be scaled independently
- **Database sharding** distributes load across multiple nodes
- **Event-driven architecture** enables loose coupling


### **Performance Optimization**

- **CQRS** separates read/write workloads
- **Multi-layer caching** reduces database load
- **Async processing** improves response times


### **Reliability \& Resilience**

- **Circuit breakers** prevent cascade failures
- **Saga patterns** ensure data consistency
- **Event sourcing** provides audit trail and replay capability


### **Operational Excellence**

- **Container orchestration** enables auto-scaling
- **Comprehensive monitoring** provides visibility
- **Infrastructure as Code** ensures reproducibility

This architecture can handle **millions of orders per day** with proper hardware provisioning and can scale both horizontally and vertically based on demand patterns. The event-driven approach ensures that even during peak loads, the system remains responsive and consistent.

### 2. **Domain-Driven Design with Clean Architecture**

**Order Aggregate with Rich Domain Model:**

```java
// order/domain/Order.java
@Entity
@Table(name = "orders")
@Data
@NoArgsConstructor
@AllArgsConstructor(access = AccessLevel.PRIVATE)
@Builder
public class Order {
    @Id
    @GeneratedValue(strategy = GenerationType.IDENTITY)
    private Long id;
    
    @Column(nullable = false, unique = true)
    private String orderNumber;
    
    @Embedded
    private Customer customer;
    
    @Embedded
    private OrderAmount amount;
    
    @Enumerated(EnumType.STRING)
    @Column(nullable = false)
    private OrderState currentState = OrderState.PENDING_PAYMENT;
    
    @CreationTimestamp
    private LocalDateTime createdAt;
    
    @UpdateTimestamp
    private LocalDateTime updatedAt;
    
    @OneToMany(mappedBy = "order", cascade = CascadeType.ALL, fetch = FetchType.LAZY)
    private List<OrderItem> items = new ArrayList<>();
    
    @OneToMany(mappedBy = "order", cascade = CascadeType.ALL, fetch = FetchType.LAZY)
    private List<OrderStateHistory> stateHistory = new ArrayList<>();
    
    @OneToMany(mappedBy = "order", cascade = CascadeType.ALL, fetch = FetchType.LAZY)
    private List<Return> returns = new ArrayList<>();
    
    // Rich domain methods
    public void processPayment(PaymentDetails paymentDetails) {
        if (!canProcessPayment()) {
            throw new InvalidOrderStateException("Order is not in a state to process payment");
        }
        
        this.currentState = OrderState.PAID;
        recordStateChange(OrderState.PENDING_PAYMENT, OrderState.PAID, "Payment processed");
        
        // Publish domain event
        DomainEventPublisher.publish(new OrderPaidEvent(this.id, paymentDetails));
    }
    
    public void startProcessing() {
        validateStateTransition(OrderState.PAID, OrderState.PROCESSING_IN_WAREHOUSE);
        this.currentState = OrderState.PROCESSING_IN_WAREHOUSE;
        recordStateChange(OrderState.PAID, OrderState.PROCESSING_IN_WAREHOUSE, "Processing started");
        
        DomainEventPublisher.publish(new OrderProcessingStartedEvent(this.id));
    }
    
    public void ship(ShippingDetails shippingDetails) {
        validateStateTransition(OrderState.PROCESSING_IN_WAREHOUSE, OrderState.SHIPPED);
        this.currentState = OrderState.SHIPPED;
        recordStateChange(OrderState.PROCESSING_IN_WAREHOUSE, OrderState.SHIPPED, "Order shipped");
        
        DomainEventPublisher.publish(new OrderShippedEvent(this.id, shippingDetails));
    }
    
    public void markAsDelivered() {
        validateStateTransition(OrderState.SHIPPED, OrderState.DELIVERED);
        this.currentState = OrderState.DELIVERED;
        recordStateChange(OrderState.SHIPPED, OrderState.DELIVERED, "Order delivered");
        
        DomainEventPublisher.publish(new OrderDeliveredEvent(this.id));
    }
    
    public boolean canBeReturned() {
        return this.currentState == OrderState.DELIVERED 
            && this.createdAt.isAfter(LocalDateTime.now().minusDays(30));
    }
    
    private boolean canProcessPayment() {
        return this.currentState == OrderState.PENDING_PAYMENT;
    }
    
    private void validateStateTransition(OrderState from, OrderState to) {
        if (this.currentState != from) {
            throw new InvalidOrderStateException(
                String.format("Cannot transition from %s to %s. Current state is %s", 
                    from, to, this.currentState));
        }
    }
    
    private void recordStateChange(OrderState from, OrderState to, String reason) {
        OrderStateHistory history = OrderStateHistory.builder()
            .order(this)
            .fromState(from)
            .toState(to)
            .reason(reason)
            .changedBy("SYSTEM") // Or actual user
            .changedAt(LocalDateTime.now())
            .build();
        
        this.stateHistory.add(history);
    }
}
```

```java
@Embeddable
@Data
@NoArgsConstructor
@AllArgsConstructor
public class OrderAmount {
    @Column(nullable = false, precision = 10, scale = 2)
    private BigDecimal subtotal;
    
    @Column(nullable = false, precision = 10, scale = 2)
    private BigDecimal tax;
    
    @Column(nullable = false, precision = 10, scale = 2)
    private BigDecimal shipping;
    
    @Column(nullable = false, precision = 10, scale = 2)
    private BigDecimal total;
    
    public static OrderAmount calculate(BigDecimal subtotal, BigDecimal taxRate, BigDecimal shippingCost) {
        BigDecimal tax = subtotal.multiply(taxRate).setScale(2, RoundingMode.HALF_UP);
        BigDecimal total = subtotal.add(tax).add(shippingCost);
        
        return new OrderAmount(subtotal, tax, shippingCost, total);
    }
}
```

### 3. **Advanced State Machine with Spring State Machine**

```java
// order/statemachine/OrderStateMachineConfig.java
@Configuration
@EnableStateMachine(name = "orderStateMachine")
@RequiredArgsConstructor
public class OrderStateMachineConfig extends StateMachineConfigurerAdapter<OrderState, OrderEvent> {
    
    private final OrderService orderService;
    private final NotificationService notificationService;
    private final InvoiceService invoiceService;
    private final ApplicationEventPublisher eventPublisher;
    
    @Override
    public void configure(StateMachineStateConfigurer<OrderState, OrderEvent> states) throws Exception {
        states
            .withStates()
            .initial(OrderState.PENDING_PAYMENT)
            .state(OrderState.PAID, paymentConfirmedAction())
            .state(OrderState.PROCESSING_IN_WAREHOUSE, processingStartedAction())
            .state(OrderState.SHIPPED, shippedAction())
            .state(OrderState.DELIVERED, deliveredAction())
            .end(OrderState.CANCELLED)
            .end(OrderState.DELIVERED);
    }
    
    @Override
    public void configure(StateMachineTransitionConfigurer<OrderState, OrderEvent> transitions) throws Exception {
        transitions
            .withExternal()
                .source(OrderState.PENDING_PAYMENT).target(OrderState.PAID)
                .event(OrderEvent.PAYMENT_RECEIVED)
                .guard(paymentValidGuard())
                .action(processPaymentAction())
            .and()
            .withExternal()
                .source(OrderState.PAID).target(OrderState.PROCESSING_IN_WAREHOUSE)
                .event(OrderEvent.START_PROCESSING)
                .guard(inventoryAvailableGuard())
            .and()
            .withExternal()
                .source(OrderState.PROCESSING_IN_WAREHOUSE).target(OrderState.SHIPPED)
                .event(OrderEvent.SHIP_ORDER)
                .action(shipOrderAction())
            .and()
            .withExternal()
                .source(OrderState.SHIPPED).target(OrderState.DELIVERED)
                .event(OrderEvent.DELIVER_ORDER)
                .action(deliverOrderAction())
            .and()
            .withExternal()
                .source(OrderState.PENDING_PAYMENT).target(OrderState.CANCELLED)
                .event(OrderEvent.CANCEL_ORDER)
            .and()
            .withExternal()
                .source(OrderState.PAID).target(OrderState.CANCELLED)
                .event(OrderEvent.CANCEL_ORDER)
                .action(refundPaymentAction());
    }
    
    @Bean
    public Guard<OrderState, OrderEvent> paymentValidGuard() {
        return context -> {
            Long orderId = (Long) context.getExtendedState().getVariables().get("orderId");
            return orderService.isPaymentValid(orderId);
        };
    }
    
    @Bean
    public Action<OrderState, OrderEvent> shipOrderAction() {
        return context -> {
            Long orderId = (Long) context.getExtendedState().getVariables().get("orderId");
            
            // Generate invoice asynchronously
            eventPublisher.publishEvent(new GenerateInvoiceEvent(orderId));
            
            // Send shipping notification
            Order order = orderService.getOrderById(orderId);
            notificationService.sendShippingNotification(order);
        };
    }
    
    @Bean
    public Action<OrderState, OrderEvent> deliverOrderAction() {
        return context -> {
            Long orderId = (Long) context.getExtendedState().getVariables().get("orderId");
            Order order = orderService.getOrderById(orderId);
            
            // Send delivery confirmation
            notificationService.sendDeliveryConfirmation(order);
            
            // Enable return option
            eventPublisher.publishEvent(new OrderDeliveredEvent(orderId));
        };
    }
}
```


### 4. **Sophisticated Service Layer with Transaction Management**

```java
// order/service/OrderService.java
@Service
@Transactional
@RequiredArgsConstructor
@Slf4j
public class OrderService {
    
    private final OrderRepository orderRepository;
    private final OrderStateHistoryRepository stateHistoryRepository;
    private final InventoryService inventoryService;
    private final PaymentService paymentService;
    private final StateMachine<OrderState, OrderEvent> orderStateMachine;
    private final ApplicationEventPublisher eventPublisher;
    
    @Transactional
    public Order createOrder(CreateOrderRequest request) {
        log.info("Creating order for customer: {}", request.getCustomerEmail());
        
        // Validate inventory availability
        List<OrderItem> items = validateAndCreateOrderItems(request.getItems());
        
        // Calculate amounts
        OrderAmount amount = calculateOrderAmount(items);
        
        // Create order
        Order order = Order.builder()
            .orderNumber(generateOrderNumber())
            .customer(Customer.builder()
                .email(request.getCustomerEmail())
                .firstName(request.getFirstName())
                .lastName(request.getLastName())
                .address(request.getAddress())
                .build())
            .amount(amount)
            .items(items)
            .currentState(OrderState.PENDING_PAYMENT)
            .build();
            
        order = orderRepository.save(order);
        
        // Reserve inventory
        inventoryService.reserveItems(order.getId(), items);
        
        // Publish domain event
        eventPublisher.publishEvent(new OrderCreatedEvent(order));
        
        log.info("Order created successfully with ID: {}", order.getId());
        return order;
    }
    
    @Transactional
    public Order processPayment(Long orderId, PaymentRequest paymentRequest) {
        Order order = getOrderById(orderId);
        
        try {
            // Process payment through payment service
            PaymentResult paymentResult = paymentService.processPayment(
                order.getAmount().getTotal(), 
                paymentRequest
            );
            
            if (paymentResult.isSuccessful()) {
                // Update order state through state machine
                orderStateMachine.getExtendedState().getVariables().put("orderId", orderId);
                orderStateMachine.sendEvent(OrderEvent.PAYMENT_RECEIVED);
                
                order.processPayment(paymentResult.getPaymentDetails());
                order = orderRepository.save(order);
                
                // Automatically start processing
                startProcessing(orderId);
                
                return order;
            } else {
                throw new PaymentProcessingException("Payment failed: " + paymentResult.getErrorMessage());
            }
            
        } catch (Exception e) {
            // Release inventory reservation on payment failure
            inventoryService.releaseReservation(orderId);
            throw e;
        }
    }
    
    @Transactional
    public Order transitionOrderState(Long orderId, OrderEvent event) {
        Order order = getOrderById(orderId);
        OrderState previousState = order.getCurrentState();
        
        // Configure state machine with order context
        orderStateMachine.getExtendedState().getVariables().put("orderId", orderId);
        
        boolean transitionSuccessful = orderStateMachine.sendEvent(event);
        
        if (!transitionSuccessful) {
            throw new InvalidStateTransitionException(
                String.format("Cannot transition from %s with event %s", previousState, event));
        }
        
        OrderState newState = orderStateMachine.getState().getId();
        
        if (!previousState.equals(newState)) {
            order.setCurrentState(newState);
            order = orderRepository.save(order);
            
            log.info("Order {} transitioned from {} to {} via event {}", 
                orderId, previousState, newState, event);
        }
        
        return order;
    }
    
    @Transactional(readOnly = true)
    public Order getOrderById(Long orderId) {
        return orderRepository.findByIdWithDetails(orderId)
            .orElseThrow(() -> new OrderNotFoundException("Order not found with ID: " + orderId));
    }
    
    @Transactional(readOnly = true)
    @Cacheable(value = "customerOrders", key = "#customerEmail")
    public List<OrderSummaryDTO> getCustomerOrders(String customerEmail) {
        return orderRepository.findOrderSummariesByCustomerEmail(customerEmail);
    }
    
    private String generateOrderNumber() {
        return "ORD-" + System.currentTimeMillis() + "-" + 
               ThreadLocalRandom.current().nextInt(1000, 9999);
    }
    
    private OrderAmount calculateOrderAmount(List<OrderItem> items) {
        BigDecimal subtotal = items.stream()
            .map(item -> item.getPrice().multiply(BigDecimal.valueOf(item.getQuantity())))
            .reduce(BigDecimal.ZERO, BigDecimal::add);
            
        BigDecimal taxRate = new BigDecimal("0.08"); // 8% tax
        BigDecimal shippingCost = new BigDecimal("15.00");
        
        return OrderAmount.calculate(subtotal, taxRate, shippingCost);
    }
}
```

```java
// Event handlers for cross-module communication
@Component
@EventListener
@Async
@RequiredArgsConstructor
@Slf4j
public class OrderEventHandler {
    
    private final InvoiceService invoiceService;
    private final NotificationService notificationService;
    private final AuditService auditService;
    
    @EventListener
    @Async("taskExecutor")
    public void handleOrderShipped(OrderShippedEvent event) {
        log.info("Handling order shipped event for order: {}", event.getOrderId());
        
        try {
            // Generate invoice asynchronously
            invoiceService.generateInvoiceAsync(event.getOrderId());
            
            // Send shipping notification
            notificationService.sendShippingNotificationAsync(event.getOrderId(), event.getTrackingNumber());
            
            // Audit the event
            auditService.recordEvent(event);
            
        } catch (Exception e) {
            log.error("Error handling order shipped event for order: {}", event.getOrderId(), e);
        }
    }
    
    @EventListener
    @Async("taskExecutor")
    public void handleOrderDelivered(OrderDeliveredEvent event) {
        log.info("Handling order delivered event for order: {}", event.getOrderId());
        
        try {
            // Enable return option
            notificationService.sendDeliveryConfirmationWithReturnInfo(event.getOrderId());
            
            // Start return window timer
            scheduleReturnWindowExpiry(event.getOrderId());
            
        } catch (Exception e) {
            log.error("Error handling order delivered event for order: {}", event.getOrderId(), e);
        }
    }
}
```

### 6. **Advanced Caching Strategy**

```java
// shared/config/CacheConfig.java
@Configuration
@EnableCaching
@RequiredArgsConstructor
public class CacheConfig {
    
    @Bean
    @Primary
    public CacheManager cacheManager() {
        return new CompositeCacheManager(
            caffeineCacheManager(),
            redisCacheManager()
        );
    }
    
    @Bean
    public CacheManager caffeineCacheManager() {
        CaffeineCacheManager manager = new CaffeineCacheManager();
        manager.setCaffeine(Caffeine.newBuilder()
            .maximumSize(10_000)
            .expireAfterWrite(5, TimeUnit.MINUTES)
            .expireAfterAccess(2, TimeUnit.MINUTES)
            .recordStats());
        manager.setCacheNames(Arrays.asList("orders", "customers", "order-summaries"));
        return manager;
    }
    
    @Bean
    public CacheManager redisCacheManager() {
        RedisCacheConfiguration config = RedisCacheConfiguration.defaultCacheConfig()
            .entryTtl(Duration.ofMinutes(30))
            .disableCachingNullValues()
            .serializeKeysWith(RedisSerializationContext.SerializationPair.fromSerializer(new StringRedisSerializer()))
            .serializeValuesWith(RedisSerializationContext.SerializationPair.fromSerializer(new GenericJackson2JsonRedisSerializer()));
            
        Map<String, RedisCacheConfiguration> cacheConfigurations = new HashMap<>();
        cacheConfigurations.put("customerOrders", config.entryTtl(Duration.ofHours(2)));
        cacheConfigurations.put("orderHistory", config.entryTtl(Duration.ofDays(1)));
        
        return RedisCacheManager.builder(redisConnectionFactory())
            .cacheDefaults(config)
            .withInitialCacheConfigurations(cacheConfigurations)
            .build();
    }
}

// Cache management service
@Service
@RequiredArgsConstructor
public class CacheManagementService {
    
    private final CacheManager cacheManager;
    
    @EventListener
    public void handleOrderStateChanged(OrderStateChangedEvent event) {
        // Invalidate relevant caches when order state changes
        evictOrderCaches(event.getOrderId(), event.getCustomerEmail());
    }
    
    private void evictOrderCaches(Long orderId, String customerEmail) {
        Optional.ofNullable(cacheManager.getCache("orders"))
            .ifPresent(cache -> cache.evict(orderId));
            
        Optional.ofNullable(cacheManager.getCache("customerOrders"))
            .ifPresent(cache -> cache.evict(customerEmail));
    }
}
```

### 8. **Async Processing with Spring Async**

```java
// shared/config/AsyncConfig.java
@Configuration
@EnableAsync
public class AsyncConfig {
    
    @Bean(name = "taskExecutor")
    public ThreadPoolTaskExecutor taskExecutor() {
        ThreadPoolTaskExecutor executor = new ThreadPoolTaskExecutor();
        executor.setCorePoolSize(10);
        executor.setMaxPoolSize(50);
        executor.setQueueCapacity(100);
        executor.setThreadNamePrefix("ArticuratedAsync-");
        executor.setRejectedExecutionHandler(new ThreadPoolExecutor.CallerRunsPolicy());
        executor.setWaitForTasksToCompleteOnShutdown(true);
        executor.setAwaitTerminationSeconds(60);
        executor.initialize();
        return executor;
    }
    
    @Bean(name = "notificationExecutor")
    public ThreadPoolTaskExecutor notificationExecutor() {
        ThreadPoolTaskExecutor executor = new ThreadPoolTaskExecutor();
        executor.setCorePoolSize(5);
        executor.setMaxPoolSize(20);
        executor.setQueueCapacity(50);
        executor.setThreadNamePrefix("NotificationAsync-");
        executor.initialize();
        return executor;
    }
}

// Async service implementations
@Service
@RequiredArgsConstructor
@Slf4j
public class AsyncInvoiceService {
    
    private final InvoiceService invoiceService;
    private final NotificationService notificationService;
    
    @Async("taskExecutor")
    @Retryable(value = {Exception.class}, maxAttempts = 3, backoff = @Backoff(delay = 1000))
    public CompletableFuture<Void> generateInvoiceAsync(Long orderId) {
        log.info("Generating invoice asynchronously for order: {}", orderId);
        
        try {
            byte[] invoicePdf = invoiceService.generateInvoicePdf(orderId);
            String fileName = "invoice-" + orderId + ".pdf";
            
            // Store invoice
            invoiceService.storeInvoice(orderId, fileName, invoicePdf);
            
            // Send email with invoice
            notificationService.sendInvoiceEmail(orderId, fileName, invoicePdf);
            
            log.info("Invoice generated and sent successfully for order: {}", orderId);
            return CompletableFuture.completedFuture(null);
            
        } catch (Exception e) {
            log.error("Failed to generate invoice for order: {}", orderId, e);
            throw e;
        }
    }
}
```

✅ **Clean Architecture** with domain-driven design
✅ **Rich domain models** with business logic encapsulation
✅ **Advanced state machine** with guards and actions
✅ **Event-driven internal communication** for loose coupling
✅ **Multi-layer caching** for performance

✅ **Proper transaction management** with rollback capabilities
✅ **Database optimization** with connection pooling

This approach gives you the **benefits of microservices patterns** (modularity, testability, scalability) while maintaining the **simplicity of a monolith** (single deployment, easier debugging, ACID transactions).

## 1. README.md

```markdown
# ArtiCurated Order Management System

A sophisticated Spring Boot application implementing a state machine-driven order management system for a boutique online marketplace specializing in high-value artisanal goods.

## Overview

This system manages the complete lifecycle of orders from payment processing to delivery, including a multi-step returns workflow with manual approval processes. Built with scalability and maintainability in mind using modern Spring Boot practices.

## Tech Stack

- **Framework**: Spring Boot 3.2.0
- **Java Version**: 17
- **Database**: PostgreSQL 15
- **Message Broker**: RabbitMQ 3.12
- **Caching**: Redis 7.0
- **State Machine**: Spring State Machine
- **Documentation**: OpenAPI 3.0 (Swagger)
- **Testing**: JUnit 5, Testcontainers, Mockito
- **Build Tool**: Maven 3.9+

## Quick Start

### Prerequisites

- Docker and Docker Compose
- Java 17+ (if running locally)
- Maven 3.9+ (if building locally)

### Running with Docker (Recommended)

1. Clone the repository:
```

git clone <your-repo-url>
cd articurated-order-system

```

2. Start all services:
```

docker-compose up -d

```

3. Wait for all services to be healthy (about 2-3 minutes):
```

docker-compose ps

```

4. Access the application:
- **API Documentation**: http://localhost:8080/swagger-ui.html
- **Application Health**: http://localhost:8080/actuator/health
- **RabbitMQ Management**: http://localhost:15672 (admin/password)
- **Database**: localhost:5432 (articurated/password)

### Running Locally

1. Start dependencies:
```

docker-compose up -d db rabbitmq redis

```

2. Set environment variables:
```

export SPRING_PROFILES_ACTIVE=local
export DB_HOST=localhost
export RABBITMQ_HOST=localhost
export REDIS_HOST=localhost

```

3. Run the application:
```

./mvnw spring-boot:run

```

## Key Modules Explanation

### 1. Shared Module (`shared/`)

Contains cross-cutting concerns used across all domains:

- **config/**: Application configuration (Database, Cache, Async, etc.)
- **exception/**: Global exception handlers and custom exceptions
- **security/**: Authentication and authorization components
- **audit/**: Audit trail functionality for compliance
- **events/**: Base domain event classes and event publishing
- **utils/**: Common utility classes and helpers

### 2. Order Module (`order/`)

Core business domain for managing order lifecycle:

- **domain/Order.java**: Rich domain entity with business logic
- **domain/OrderState.java**: Enum defining order states
- **domain/OrderEvent.java**: Enum defining state transition events
- **statemachine/OrderStateMachineConfig.java**: State machine configuration
- **service/OrderService.java**: Business logic for order operations
- **controller/OrderController.java**: REST API endpoints
- **repository/OrderRepository.java**: Data access with custom queries

### 3. Returns Module (`returns/`)

Handles the multi-step return workflow:

- **domain/Return.java**: Return entity with approval workflow
- **statemachine/ReturnStateMachineConfig.java**: Return state machine
- **service/ReturnService.java**: Return business logic
- **controller/ReturnController.java**: Return API endpoints

### 4. Payment Module (`payment/`)

Manages payment processing:

- **service/PaymentService.java**: Payment orchestration
- **gateway/PaymentGatewayService.java**: External payment integration
- **domain/PaymentResult.java**: Payment result value object

### 5. Notification Module (`notification/`)

Handles all customer communications:

- **service/NotificationService.java**: Notification orchestration
- **provider/EmailProvider.java**: Email service implementation
- **template/**: Email templates for different events

### 6. Messaging Module (`messaging/`)

Async message processing:

- **config/RabbitMQConfig.java**: Queue and exchange configuration
- **producer/MessageProducer.java**: Message publishing
- **consumer/InvoiceMessageConsumer.java**: Invoice generation worker
- **consumer/RefundMessageConsumer.java**: Refund processing worker
```

## 3. WORKFLOW_DESIGN.md

```markdown
# Workflow Design Document

This document explains the implementation details of the ArtiCurated Order Management System, including state machine diagrams and database schema.

## State Machine Workflows

### Order State Machine

```

Order Lifecycle State Diagram

    ┌─────────────────┐
    │ PENDING_PAYMENT │ ◄──── Initial State
    └─────────────────┘
             │
             │ PAYMENT_RECEIVED
             ▼
    ┌─────────────────┐
    │      PAID       │
    └─────────────────┘
             │
             │ START_PROCESSING
             ▼
    ┌─────────────────┐
    │ PROCESSING_IN_  │
    │   WAREHOUSE     │
    └─────────────────┘
             │
             │ SHIP_ORDER (triggers invoice generation)
             ▼
    ┌─────────────────┐
    │    SHIPPED      │
    └─────────────────┘
             │
             │ DELIVER_ORDER
             ▼
    ┌─────────────────┐
    │   DELIVERED     │ ◄──── End State (enables returns)
    └─────────────────┘
    
    Cancellation Paths:
    PENDING_PAYMENT ──CANCEL_ORDER──► CANCELLED
    PAID ──CANCEL_ORDER──► CANCELLED (with refund)
    ```

#### Order State Transitions

| From State | Event | To State | Validations | Side Effects |
|------------|-------|----------|-------------|--------------|
| PENDING_PAYMENT | PAYMENT_RECEIVED | PAID | Payment validation | Reserve inventory |
| PAID | START_PROCESSING | PROCESSING_IN_WAREHOUSE | Inventory available | Update inventory |
| PROCESSING_IN_WAREHOUSE | SHIP_ORDER | SHIPPED | Items packed | Generate invoice, Send notification |
| SHIPPED | DELIVER_ORDER | DELIVERED | Delivery confirmed | Enable returns, Send confirmation |
| PENDING_PAYMENT | CANCEL_ORDER | CANCELLED | Before processing | Release reservation |
| PAID | CANCEL_ORDER | CANCELLED | Before shipping | Refund payment |

### Return State Machine

```

Return Lifecycle State Diagram

    ┌─────────────────┐
    │   REQUESTED     │ ◄──── Initial State (customer initiates)
    └─────────────────┘
             │
             │ APPROVE_RETURN / REJECT_RETURN
             ▼
    ┌─────────────────┐         ┌─────────────────┐
    │    APPROVED     │         │    REJECTED     │ ◄──── End State
    └─────────────────┘         └─────────────────┘
             │
             │ CUSTOMER_SHIPS
             ▼
    ┌─────────────────┐
    │   IN_TRANSIT    │
    └─────────────────┘
             │
             │ WAREHOUSE_RECEIVES
             ▼
    ┌─────────────────┐
    │    RECEIVED     │
    └─────────────────┘
             │
             │ PROCESS_REFUND (triggers refund processing)
             ▼
    ┌─────────────────┐
    │   COMPLETED     │ ◄──── End State
    └─────────────────┘
    ```

#### Return State Transitions

| From State | Event | To State | Validations | Side Effects |
|------------|-------|----------|-------------|--------------|
| REQUESTED | APPROVE_RETURN | APPROVED | Manager approval | Send return label |
| REQUESTED | REJECT_RETURN | REJECTED | Manager decision | Send rejection notice |
| APPROVED | CUSTOMER_SHIPS | IN_TRANSIT | Tracking provided | Update tracking |
| IN_TRANSIT | WAREHOUSE_RECEIVES | RECEIVED | Item inspection | Quality check |
| RECEIVED | PROCESS_REFUND | COMPLETED | Refund validation | Process refund, Update inventory |

## Database Schema

### Core Tables

```

-- Orders table
CREATE TABLE orders (
id BIGSERIAL PRIMARY KEY,
order_number VARCHAR(50) UNIQUE NOT NULL,
customer_email VARCHAR(255) NOT NULL,
customer_first_name VARCHAR(100) NOT NULL,
customer_last_name VARCHAR(100) NOT NULL,
subtotal DECIMAL(10,2) NOT NULL,
tax DECIMAL(10,2) NOT NULL,
shipping DECIMAL(10,2) NOT NULL,
total DECIMAL(10,2) NOT NULL,
current_state VARCHAR(50) NOT NULL DEFAULT 'PENDING_PAYMENT',
created_at TIMESTAMP DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP,
updated_at TIMESTAMP DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP,

    -- Address embedded
    street VARCHAR(255),
    city VARCHAR(100),
    state VARCHAR(50),
    zip_code VARCHAR(20),
    country VARCHAR(50)
    );

-- Order Items table
CREATE TABLE order_items (
id BIGSERIAL PRIMARY KEY,
order_id BIGINT REFERENCES orders(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
product_name VARCHAR(255) NOT NULL,
price DECIMAL(10,2) NOT NULL,
quantity INTEGER NOT NULL,
total DECIMAL(10,2) NOT NULL
);

-- Order State History table (for audit trail)
CREATE TABLE order_state_history (
id BIGSERIAL PRIMARY KEY,
order_id BIGINT REFERENCES orders(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
from_state VARCHAR(50),
to_state VARCHAR(50) NOT NULL,
reason VARCHAR(500),
changed_by VARCHAR(100) DEFAULT 'SYSTEM',
changed_at TIMESTAMP DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP
);

-- Returns table
CREATE TABLE returns (
id BIGSERIAL PRIMARY KEY,
return_number VARCHAR(50) UNIQUE NOT NULL,
order_id BIGINT REFERENCES orders(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
reason VARCHAR(500) NOT NULL,
current_state VARCHAR(50) NOT NULL DEFAULT 'REQUESTED',
approved_by VARCHAR(100),
tracking_number VARCHAR(100),
refund_amount DECIMAL(10,2),
created_at TIMESTAMP DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP,
updated_at TIMESTAMP DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP
);

-- Return State History table
CREATE TABLE return_state_history (
id BIGSERIAL PRIMARY KEY,
return_id BIGINT REFERENCES returns(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
from_state VARCHAR(50),
to_state VARCHAR(50) NOT NULL,
reason VARCHAR(500),
changed_by VARCHAR(100) DEFAULT 'SYSTEM',
changed_at TIMESTAMP DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP
);

-- Payment records table
CREATE TABLE payment_records (
id BIGSERIAL PRIMARY KEY,
order_id BIGINT REFERENCES orders(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
payment_method VARCHAR(50) NOT NULL,
amount DECIMAL(10,2) NOT NULL,
status VARCHAR(50) NOT NULL,
transaction_id VARCHAR(100),
gateway_response TEXT,
processed_at TIMESTAMP DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP
);

-- Inventory table
CREATE TABLE inventory (
id BIGSERIAL PRIMARY KEY,
product_name VARCHAR(255) UNIQUE NOT NULL,
available_quantity INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
reserved_quantity INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
price DECIMAL(10,2) NOT NULL,
created_at TIMESTAMP DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP,
updated_at TIMESTAMP DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP
);

-- Inventory reservations table
CREATE TABLE inventory_reservations (
id BIGSERIAL PRIMARY KEY,
order_id BIGINT REFERENCES orders(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
product_name VARCHAR(255) NOT NULL,
quantity INTEGER NOT NULL,
reserved_at TIMESTAMP DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP,
expires_at TIMESTAMP NOT NULL
);

```

### Indexes for Performance

```

-- Order indexes
CREATE INDEX idx_orders_customer_email ON orders(customer_email);
CREATE INDEX idx_orders_state ON orders(current_state);
CREATE INDEX idx_orders_created_at ON orders(created_at);
CREATE INDEX idx_orders_number ON orders(order_number);

-- Order items indexes
CREATE INDEX idx_order_items_order_id ON order_items(order_id);
CREATE INDEX idx_order_items_product ON order_items(product_name);

-- State history indexes
CREATE INDEX idx_order_history_order_id ON order_state_history(order_id);
CREATE INDEX idx_order_history_changed_at ON order_state_history(changed_at);
CREATE INDEX idx_return_history_return_id ON return_state_history(return_id);

-- Return indexes
CREATE INDEX idx_returns_order_id ON returns(order_id);
CREATE INDEX idx_returns_state ON returns(current_state);
CREATE INDEX idx_returns_number ON returns(return_number);

-- Performance indexes
CREATE INDEX idx_orders_composite ON orders(customer_email, current_state, created_at);

```

## Implementation Details

### State Machine Configuration

#### Order State Machine Guards

```

// Payment validation guard
@Bean
public Guard<OrderState, OrderEvent> paymentValidGuard() {
return context -> {
Long orderId = (Long) context.getExtendedState().getVariables().get("orderId");
PaymentRecord payment = paymentService.getPaymentRecord(orderId);
return payment != null \&\& payment.getStatus() == PaymentStatus.SUCCESSFUL;
};
}

// Inventory availability guard
@Bean
public Guard<OrderState, OrderEvent> inventoryAvailableGuard() {
return context -> {
Long orderId = (Long) context.getExtendedState().getVariables().get("orderId");
return inventoryService.isInventoryAvailable(orderId);
};
}

```

#### State Machine Actions

```

// Ship order action with side effects
@Bean
public Action<OrderState, OrderEvent> shipOrderAction() {
return context -> {
Long orderId = (Long) context.getExtendedState().getVariables().get("orderId");

        // Generate invoice asynchronously
        messageProducer.sendInvoiceGenerationMessage(orderId);
        
        // Send shipping notification
        Order order = orderService.getOrderById(orderId);
        notificationService.sendShippingNotification(order);
        
        // Update inventory
        inventoryService.confirmShipment(orderId);
    };
    }

```

### Async Background Jobs

#### Invoice Generation Worker

```

@RabbitListener(queues = RabbitMQConfig.INVOICE_QUEUE)
public void handleInvoiceGeneration(@Payload Long orderId) {
try {
// Generate PDF invoice
byte[] invoicePdf = invoiceService.generateInvoicePdf(orderId);

        // Store in file system or cloud storage
        String fileName = "invoice-" + orderId + ".pdf";
        fileStorageService.store(fileName, invoicePdf);
        
        // Send email with invoice attachment
        Order order = orderService.getOrderById(orderId);
        emailService.sendInvoiceEmail(order.getCustomer().getEmail(), fileName, invoicePdf);
        
    } catch (Exception e) {
        log.error("Failed to generate invoice for order: {}", orderId, e);
        // Implement retry logic or dead letter queue
    }
    }

```

#### Refund Processing Worker

```

@RabbitListener(queues = RabbitMQConfig.REFUND_QUEUE)
public void handleRefundProcessing(@Payload RefundRequest refundRequest) {
try {
// Call external payment gateway
RefundResult result = paymentGatewayService.processRefund(
refundRequest.getTransactionId(),
refundRequest.getAmount()
);

        if (result.isSuccessful()) {
            // Update return status
            returnService.markRefundCompleted(refundRequest.getReturnId());
            
            // Send confirmation email
            notificationService.sendRefundConfirmation(refundRequest);
        } else {
            // Handle refund failure
            returnService.markRefundFailed(refundRequest.getReturnId(), result.getErrorMessage());
        }
        
    } catch (Exception e) {
        log.error("Failed to process refund for return: {}", refundRequest.getReturnId(), e);
    }
    }

```

### Data Relationships

```

┌─────────────┐         ┌─────────────────┐         ┌─────────────┐
│   Orders    │1      *│   Order Items   │         │  Inventory  │
│             │─────────│                 │─────────│             │
│ - id        │         │ - order_id (FK) │         │ - product   │
│ - number    │         │ - product_name  │         │ - quantity  │
│ - customer  │         │ - price         │         │ - reserved  │
│ - state     │         │ - quantity      │         └─────────────┘
└─────────────┘         └─────────────────┘
│1
│
│*                ┌─────────────────┐
└─────────────────│ Order History   │
│                 │
│ - order_id (FK) │
│ - from_state    │
┌─────────────┐   │ - to_state      │
│   Returns   │   │ - timestamp     │
│             │   └─────────────────┘
│ - id        │
│ - order_id  │1        *┌─────────────────┐
│ - reason    │─────────│ Return History  │
│ - state     │         │                 │
└─────────────┘         │ - return_id(FK) │
│ - from_state    │
│ - to_state      │
│ - timestamp     │
└─────────────────┘

```

This design ensures:
- **Data integrity** through foreign key constraints
- **Audit compliance** with complete state history
- **Performance optimization** through strategic indexing
- **Scalability** through async processing
- **Reliability** through transaction management
```

## 5. docker-compose.yml

```yaml
version: '3.8'

services:
  app:
    build:
      context: .
      dockerfile: Dockerfile
    container_name: articurated-app
    ports:
      - "8080:8080"
    environment:
      - SPRING_PROFILES_ACTIVE=docker
      - DB_HOST=db
      - DB_PORT=5432
      - DB_NAME=articurated
      - DB_USERNAME=articurated
      - DB_PASSWORD=password
      - RABBITMQ_HOST=rabbitmq
      - RABBITMQ_PORT=5672
      - RABBITMQ_USERNAME=admin
      - RABBITMQ_PASSWORD=password
      - REDIS_HOST=redis
      - REDIS_PORT=6379
    depends_on:
      db:
        condition: service_healthy
      rabbitmq:
        condition: service_healthy
      redis:
        condition: service_healthy
    networks:
      - articurated-network
    restart: unless-stopped
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD", "curl", "-f", "http://localhost:8080/actuator/health"]
      interval: 30s
      timeout: 10s
      retries: 3
      start_period: 60s

  db:
    image: postgres:15-alpine
    container_name: articurated-db
    environment:
      POSTGRES_DB: articurated
      POSTGRES_USER: articurated
      POSTGRES_PASSWORD: password
      POSTGRES_INITDB_ARGS: "--encoding=UTF-8"
    ports:
      - "5432:5432"
    volumes:
      - postgres_data:/var/lib/postgresql/data
      - ./docker/postgres/init.sql:/docker-entrypoint-initdb.d/init.sql:ro
    networks:
      - articurated-network
    restart: unless-stopped
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD-SHELL", "pg_isready -U articurated -d articurated"]
      interval: 10s
      timeout: 5s
      retries: 5

  rabbitmq:
    image: rabbitmq:3.12-management-alpine
    container_name: articurated-rabbitmq
    environment:
      RABBITMQ_DEFAULT_USER: admin
      RABBITMQ_DEFAULT_PASS: password
      RABBITMQ_DEFAULT_VHOST: /
    ports:
      - "5672:5672"
      - "15672:15672"
    volumes:
      - rabbitmq_data:/var/lib/rabbitmq
      - ./docker/rabbitmq/rabbitmq.conf:/etc/rabbitmq/rabbitmq.conf:ro
    networks:
      - articurated-network
    restart: unless-stopped
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD", "rabbitmq-diagnostics", "ping"]
      interval: 30s
      timeout: 10s
      retries: 3

  redis:
    image: redis:7-alpine
    container_name: articurated-redis
    ports:
      - "6379:6379"
    volumes:
      - redis_data:/data
    networks:
      - articurated-network
    restart: unless-stopped
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD", "redis-cli", "ping"]
      interval: 10s
      timeout: 5s
      retries: 3
    command: redis-server --appendonly yes --maxmemory 256mb --maxmemory-policy allkeys-lru

  prometheus:
    image: prom/prometheus:latest
    container_name: articurated-prometheus
    ports:
      - "9090:9090"
    volumes:
      - ./docker/prometheus/prometheus.yml:/etc/prometheus/prometheus.yml:ro
      - prometheus_data:/prometheus
    command:
      - '--config.file=/etc/prometheus/prometheus.yml'
      - '--storage.tsdb.path=/prometheus'
      - '--web.console.libraries=/etc/prometheus/console_libraries'
      - '--web.console.templates=/etc/prometheus/consoles'
      - '--web.enable-lifecycle'
    networks:
      - articurated-network
    restart: unless-stopped

  grafana:
    image: grafana/grafana:latest
    container_name: articurated-grafana
    ports:
      - "3000:3000"
    environment:
      - GF_SECURITY_ADMIN_USER=admin
      - GF_SECURITY_ADMIN_PASSWORD=admin
      - GF_USERS_ALLOW_SIGN_UP=false
    volumes:
      - grafana_data:/var/lib/grafana
      - ./docker/grafana/dashboards:/etc/grafana/provisioning/dashboards:ro
      - ./docker/grafana/datasources:/etc/grafana/provisioning/datasources:ro
    networks:
      - articurated-network
    restart: unless-stopped
    depends_on:
      - prometheus

volumes:
  postgres_data:
    driver: local
  rabbitmq_data:
    driver: local
  redis_data:
    driver: local
  prometheus_data:
    driver: local
  grafana_data:
    driver: local

networks:
  articurated-network:
    driver: bridge
    ipam:
      config:
        - subnet: 172.20.0.0/16
```


## 6. CHAT_HISTORY.md

```markdown
# Chat History: Design Journey for ArtiCurated Order Management System

This document chronicles the design decisions and AI-assisted development process for the ArtiCurated Order Management System.

## Initial Requirements Analysis

### User Query
The user presented a comprehensive business scenario for ArtiCurated, a boutique online marketplace requiring:
- Complex order state management
- Multi-step returns workflow
- Asynchronous background job processing
- Complete audit trail

### AI Assistant Analysis
I analyzed the requirements and identified key technical challenges:
1. **State Machine Complexity**: Need for robust state transitions with validation
2. **Async Processing**: Non-blocking operations for invoice generation and refunds
3. **Audit Compliance**: Complete state history tracking
4. **Scalability**: Future-proof architecture design

## Architecture Decision Process

### Decision Point 1: Monolithic vs Microservices

**User Preference**: Initially asked for Spring Boot implementation, later clarified preference for monolithic design

**AI Recommendation**: 
- Initially suggested microservices for scalability
- Pivoted to "Modular Monolith" approach when user specified monolithic preference
- Reasoning: Maintains benefits of modular design while keeping deployment simplicity

**Final Decision**: Modular monolith with domain-driven design
- **Pros**: Single deployment, ACID transactions, easier debugging
- **Cons**: Potential scaling limitations (mitigated by design patterns)

### Decision Point 2: State Machine Implementation

**AI Analysis**: Compared options:
1. Manual state management with enums
2. Spring State Machine framework
3. Custom state machine implementation

**Recommendation**: Spring State Machine
- **Reasoning**: 
  - Built-in transition validation
  - Event-driven architecture support
  - Guards and actions for side effects
  - Comprehensive testing support

**Implementation Strategy**:
```

// Rich domain model approach
public class Order {
public void processPayment(PaymentDetails details) {
validateStateTransition(PENDING_PAYMENT, PAID);
// Business logic here
publishDomainEvent(new OrderPaidEvent(this.id));
}
}

```

### Decision Point 3: Async Processing Strategy

**Options Evaluated**:
1. **Spring @Async**: Simple but limited scalability
2. **RabbitMQ**: Robust message queuing
3. **Apache Kafka**: High-throughput streaming
4. **Database-based queues**: Simple deployment

**AI Recommendation**: RabbitMQ
- **Reasoning**:
  - Mature message broker
  - Excellent Spring integration
  - Supports complex routing
  - Dead letter queues for error handling
  - Management UI for monitoring

**Implementation**:
```

@RabbitListener(queues = "invoice.generation.queue")
public void generateInvoice(@Payload Long orderId) {
// Async invoice generation
}

```

### Decision Point 4: Database Design Strategy

**AI Analysis**: Considered approaches:
1. **Single table with JSON**: Simple but poor querying
2. **Normalized tables**: Good performance and integrity
3. **Event sourcing**: Complete audit trail but complex

**Final Approach**: Hybrid solution
- Normalized tables for operational data
- Separate history tables for audit trail
- Strategic indexing for performance

**Schema Design Rationale**:
```

-- Separate state history for audit compliance
CREATE TABLE order_state_history (
id BIGSERIAL PRIMARY KEY,
order_id BIGINT REFERENCES orders(id),
from_state VARCHAR(50),
to_state VARCHAR(50),
reason VARCHAR(500),
changed_by VARCHAR(100),
changed_at TIMESTAMP
);

```

### Decision Point 5: Caching Strategy

**Performance Requirements**: High read performance for customer order history

**Multi-layered Approach**:
1. **L1 Cache (Caffeine)**: Application-level, fast access
2. **L2 Cache (Redis)**: Distributed, shared across instances
3. **Database optimization**: Proper indexing and query optimization

**AI Reasoning**: 
- Different cache layers serve different purposes
- Caffeine for frequently accessed small objects
- Redis for customer-specific data that needs sharing
```

```
## Performance and Scalability Considerations

### Database Optimization Decisions

**AI Analysis**: Identified potential bottlenecks:

2. Customer order lookups
3. State transition validations

**Optimization Strategy**:
```

-- Composite index for common query patterns
CREATE INDEX idx_orders_composite ON orders(customer_email, current_state, created_at);

-- Separate index for state transitions
CREATE INDEX idx_order_history_order_id ON order_state_history(order_id);

```

### Connection Pool Tuning

**HikariCP Configuration**:
```

spring:
datasource:
hikari:
maximum-pool-size: 20
minimum-idle: 5
connection-timeout: 30000
leak-detection-threshold: 60000

```

**AI Reasoning**: Conservative settings for monolithic deployment, can scale with load testing feedback

## Security and Compliance Decisions

### Audit Trail Implementation

**Compliance Requirement**: Complete state change history

**Implementation Strategy**:
1. **Automatic history recording**: Via JPA lifecycle events
2. **Immutable history records**: No updates allowed
3. **User attribution**: Track who made changes
4. **Timestamp precision**: Microsecond-level timestamps

### Data Privacy Considerations

**GDPR Compliance Planning**:
- Customer data anonymization capability
- Data retention policies
- Audit log protection
```

Here's a comprehensive unit test example to achieve high coverage:

```java
// OrderServiceTest.java
@ExtendWith(MockitoExtension.class)
class OrderServiceTest {
    
    @Mock
    private OrderRepository orderRepository;
    
    @Mock
    private OrderStateHistoryRepository stateHistoryRepository;
    
    @Mock
    private InventoryService inventoryService;
    
    @Mock
    private PaymentService paymentService;
    
    @Mock
    private StateMachine<OrderState, OrderEvent> orderStateMachine;
    
    @Mock
    private ApplicationEventPublisher eventPublisher;
    
    @InjectMocks
    private OrderService orderService;
    
    @Test
    void createOrder_ValidRequest_ReturnsCreatedOrder() {
        // Given
        CreateOrderRequest request = CreateOrderRequest.builder()
            .customerEmail("test@example.com")
            .firstName("John")
            .lastName("Doe")
            .items(List.of(OrderItemRequest.builder()
                .productName("Test Product")
                .price(new BigDecimal("99.99"))
                .quantity(1)
                .build()))
            .address(Address.builder()
                .street("123 Test St")
                .city("Test City")
                .state("TS")
                .zipCode("12345")
                .country("USA")
                .build())
            .build();
            
        Order savedOrder = Order.builder()
            .id(1L)
            .orderNumber("ORD-TEST-001")
            .currentState(OrderState.PENDING_PAYMENT)
            .build();
            
        when(orderRepository.save(any(Order.class))).thenReturn(savedOrder);
        when(inventoryService.validateAndCreateOrderItems(any())).thenReturn(new ArrayList<>());
        
        // When
        Order result = orderService.createOrder(request);
        
        // Then
        assertThat(result).isNotNull();
        assertThat(result.getCurrentState()).isEqualTo(OrderState.PENDING_PAYMENT);
        verify(orderRepository).save(any(Order.class));
        verify(eventPublisher).publishEvent(any(OrderCreatedEvent.class));
    }
    
    @Test
    void processPayment_ValidPayment_TransitionsToProcessing() {
        // Given
        Long orderId = 1L;
        PaymentRequest paymentRequest = PaymentRequest.builder()
            .paymentMethod("CREDIT_CARD")
            .cardNumber("4111111111111111")
            .build();
            
        Order order = Order.builder()
            .id(orderId)
            .currentState(OrderState.PENDING_PAYMENT)
            .build();
            
        PaymentResult paymentResult = PaymentResult.builder()
            .successful(true)
            .transactionId("TXN-123")
            .build();
            
        when(orderRepository.findByIdWithDetails(orderId)).thenReturn(Optional.of(order));
        when(paymentService.processPayment(any(), any())).thenReturn(paymentResult);
        when(orderRepository.save(any(Order.class))).thenReturn(order);
        
        // When
        Order result = orderService.processPayment(orderId, paymentRequest);
        
        // Then
        verify(paymentService).processPayment(any(), eq(paymentRequest));
        verify(orderStateMachine).sendEvent(OrderEvent.PAYMENT_RECEIVED);
        verify(orderRepository, times(2)).save(any(Order.class));
    }
}
```

## Key Design Principles Applied

### 1. **Domain-Driven Design (DDD)**[^5_1][^5_2]

- Each module represents a **bounded context**
- Rich domain models with business logic
- Clear module boundaries with public APIs


### 2. **Package by Feature**[^5_2][^5_3]

- All related classes grouped by business domain
- Controllers, services, and repositories co-located
- Easy to understand and navigate


### 3. **Modular Monolith Architecture**[^5_4][^5_5][^5_6]

- Independent deployable modules
- Event-driven communication between modules
- Shared infrastructure through common module


### 4. **Clean Architecture Layers**[^5_7][^5_2]

```
┌─── Controllers (API Layer)
├─── Services (Business Logic)
├─── Repositories (Data Access)
└─── Domain (Core Business Rules)
```


### 5. **Configuration by Environment**[^5_8]

- Profile-specific configurations
- Environment variable support
- Docker-ready setup


## Module Dependencies \& Communication

```
┌─────────────┐    ┌─────────────┐    ┌─────────────┐
│   Order     │────│   Payment   │────│  Inventory  │
│   Module    │    │   Module    │    │   Module    │
└─────────────┘    └─────────────┘    └─────────────┘
       │                   │                   │
       └───────────────────┼───────────────────┘
                           │
                  ┌─────────────┐
                  │   Shared    │
                  │   Module    │
                  └─────────────┘
                           │
       ┌───────────────────┼───────────────────┐
       │                   │                   │
┌─────────────┐    ┌─────────────┐    ┌─────────────┐
│   Returns   │    │Notification │    │  Messaging  │
│   Module    │    │   Module    │    │   Module    │
└─────────────┘    └─────────────┘    └─────────────┘
```


## Benefits of This Structure

### ✅ **Scalability**

- **Horizontal scaling** ready with stateless design
- **Database sharding** support through module separation
- **Async processing** for non-blocking operations


### ✅ **Maintainability**[^5_7][^5_2]

- **Clear module boundaries** reduce coupling
- **Domain-focused organization** improves understanding
- **Rich domain models** encapsulate business logic


### ✅ **Testability**[^5_9]

- **Module-level testing** with isolated components
- **Integration tests** with Testcontainers
- **High test coverage** through comprehensive test suite


### ✅ **Future-Proof Architecture**[^5_5][^5_6]

- **Easy migration to microservices** when needed
- **Event-driven communication** enables loose coupling
- **Modular design** supports independent development

This structure follows the **latest Spring Boot 3.x best practices** while providing a solid foundation for your ArtiCurated order management system that can scale from startup to enterprise level.[^5_10][^5_1]

### 2. **Minimal State Machine Configuration** (Core Requirement)

```java
// order/statemachine/OrderStateMachineConfig.java
@Configuration
@EnableStateMachine
@RequiredArgsConstructor
public class OrderStateMachineConfig extends StateMachineConfigurerAdapter<OrderState, OrderEvent> {
    
    private final ApplicationEventPublisher eventPublisher;
    
    @Override
    public void configure(StateMachineStateConfigurer<OrderState, OrderEvent> states) throws Exception {
        states
            .withStates()
            .initial(OrderState.PENDING_PAYMENT)
            .states(EnumSet.allOf(OrderState.class));
    }
    
    @Override
    public void configure(StateMachineTransitionConfigurer<OrderState, OrderEvent> transitions) throws Exception {
        transitions
            .withExternal()
                .source(OrderState.PENDING_PAYMENT).target(OrderState.PAID)
                .event(OrderEvent.PAYMENT_RECEIVED)
            .and()
            .withExternal()
                .source(OrderState.PAID).target(OrderState.PROCESSING_IN_WAREHOUSE)
                .event(OrderEvent.START_PROCESSING)
            .and()
            .withExternal()
                .source(OrderState.PROCESSING_IN_WAREHOUSE).target(OrderState.SHIPPED)
                .event(OrderEvent.SHIP_ORDER)
                .action(shipOrderAction())
            .and()
            .withExternal()
                .source(OrderState.SHIPPED).target(OrderState.DELIVERED)
                .event(OrderEvent.DELIVER_ORDER);
    }
    
    @Bean
    public Action<OrderState, OrderEvent> shipOrderAction() {
        return context -> {
            Long orderId = (Long) context.getExtendedState().getVariables().get("orderId");
            eventPublisher.publishEvent(new GenerateInvoiceEvent(orderId));
        };
    }
}

// returns/statemachine/ReturnStateMachineConfig.java
@Configuration
@EnableStateMachine(name = "returnStateMachine")
@RequiredArgsConstructor
public class ReturnStateMachineConfig extends StateMachineConfigurerAdapter<ReturnState, ReturnEvent> {
    
    private final ApplicationEventPublisher eventPublisher;
    
    @Override
    public void configure(StateMachineTransitionConfigurer<ReturnState, ReturnEvent> transitions) throws Exception {
        transitions
            .withExternal()
                .source(ReturnState.REQUESTED).target(ReturnState.APPROVED)
                .event(ReturnEvent.APPROVE)
            .and()
            .withExternal()
                .source(ReturnState.RECEIVED).target(ReturnState.COMPLETED)
                .event(ReturnEvent.PROCESS_REFUND)
                .action(processRefundAction());
    }
    
    @Bean
    public Action<ReturnState, ReturnEvent> processRefundAction() {
        return context -> {
            Long returnId = (Long) context.getExtendedState().getVariables().get("returnId");
            eventPublisher.publishEvent(new ProcessRefundEvent(returnId));
        };
    }
}
```


### 3. **Essential Services** (Business Logic)

```java
// order/service/OrderService.java
@Service
@Transactional
@RequiredArgsConstructor
@Slf4j
public class OrderService {
    
    private final OrderRepository orderRepository;
    private final OrderStateHistoryRepository stateHistoryRepository;
    private final StateMachine<OrderState, OrderEvent> stateMachine;
    
    public Order createOrder(CreateOrderRequest request) {
        Order order = Order.builder()
            .orderNumber(generateOrderNumber())
            .customerEmail(request.getCustomerEmail())
            .totalAmount(request.getTotalAmount())
            .currentState(OrderState.PENDING_PAYMENT)
            .build();
            
        order = orderRepository.save(order);
        recordStateChange(order, null, OrderState.PENDING_PAYMENT, "Order created");
        
        return order;
    }
    
    public Order transitionOrderState(Long orderId, OrderEvent event) {
        Order order = getOrderById(orderId);
        OrderState previousState = order.getCurrentState();
        
        stateMachine.getExtendedState().getVariables().put("orderId", orderId);
        boolean success = stateMachine.sendEvent(event);
        
        if (success) {
            OrderState newState = stateMachine.getState().getId();
            order.setCurrentState(newState);
            order = orderRepository.save(order);
            recordStateChange(order, previousState, newState, "State transition via " + event);
        }
        
        return order;
    }
    
    public Order getOrderById(Long orderId) {
        return orderRepository.findById(orderId)
            .orElseThrow(() -> new OrderNotFoundException("Order not found: " + orderId));
    }
    
    private void recordStateChange(Order order, OrderState from, OrderState to, String reason) {
        OrderStateHistory history = OrderStateHistory.builder()
            .order(order)
            .fromState(from)
            .toState(to)
            .reason(reason)
            .changedAt(LocalDateTime.now())
            .build();
        stateHistoryRepository.save(history);
    }
    
    private String generateOrderNumber() {
        return "ORD-" + System.currentTimeMillis();
    }
}
```


### 4. **Minimal Async Processing** (Background Jobs)

```java
// shared/config/RabbitMQConfig.java
@Configuration
@EnableRabbit
public class RabbitMQConfig {
    
    public static final String INVOICE_QUEUE = "invoice.generation";
    public static final String REFUND_QUEUE = "refund.processing";
    
    @Bean
    public Queue invoiceQueue() {
        return QueueBuilder.durable(INVOICE_QUEUE).build();
    }
    
    @Bean
    public Queue refundQueue() {
        return QueueBuilder.durable(REFUND_QUEUE).build();
    }
    
    @Bean
    public RabbitTemplate rabbitTemplate(ConnectionFactory connectionFactory) {
        return new RabbitTemplate(connectionFactory);
    }
}

// messaging/producer/MessageProducer.java
@Component
@RequiredArgsConstructor
@Slf4j
public class MessageProducer {
    
    private final RabbitTemplate rabbitTemplate;
    
    public void sendInvoiceGenerationMessage(Long orderId) {
        log.info("Sending invoice generation message for order: {}", orderId);
        rabbitTemplate.convertAndSend(RabbitMQConfig.INVOICE_QUEUE, orderId);
    }
    
    public void sendRefundProcessingMessage(Long returnId) {
        log.info("Sending refund processing message for return: {}", returnId);
        rabbitTemplate.convertAndSend(RabbitMQConfig.REFUND_QUEUE, returnId);
    }
}

// messaging/consumer/InvoiceMessageConsumer.java
@Component
@RequiredArgsConstructor
@Slf4j
public class InvoiceMessageConsumer {
    
    private final OrderService orderService;
    
    @RabbitListener(queues = RabbitMQConfig.INVOICE_QUEUE)
    public void handleInvoiceGeneration(@Payload Long orderId) {
        log.info("Processing invoice generation for order: {}", orderId);
        
        try {
            // Simulate PDF generation
            generateDummyPDF(orderId);
            
            // Simulate email sending
            simulateEmailSending(orderId);
            
            log.info("Invoice generated and sent for order: {}", orderId);
        } catch (Exception e) {
            log.error("Failed to generate invoice for order: {}", orderId, e);
        }
    }
    
    private void generateDummyPDF(Long orderId) {
        // Simple PDF generation simulation
        log.info("Generating PDF invoice for order: {}", orderId);
        // You can add actual PDF generation here using libraries like iText
    }
    
    private void simulateEmailSending(Long orderId) {
        log.info("Sending invoice email for order: {}", orderId);
        // Simulate email sending delay
        try {
            Thread.sleep(1000);
        } catch (InterruptedException e) {
            Thread.currentThread().interrupt();
        }
    }
}

// messaging/consumer/RefundMessageConsumer.java
@Component
@RequiredArgsConstructor
@Slf4j
public class RefundMessageConsumer {
    
    @RabbitListener(queues = RabbitMQConfig.REFUND_QUEUE)
    public void handleRefundProcessing(@Payload Long returnId) {
        log.info("Processing refund for return: {}", returnId);
        
        try {
            // Simulate payment gateway call
            simulatePaymentGatewayCall(returnId);
            
            log.info("Refund processed successfully for return: {}", returnId);
        } catch (Exception e) {
            log.error("Failed to process refund for return: {}", returnId, e);
        }
    }
    
    private void simulatePaymentGatewayCall(Long returnId) {
        log.info("Calling payment gateway for refund, return: {}", returnId);
        // Simulate API call delay
        try {
            Thread.sleep(2000);
        } catch (InterruptedException e) {
            Thread.currentThread().interrupt();
        }
    }
}
```

### 5. **Essential Controllers** (API Layer)

```java
// order/controller/OrderController.java
@RestController
@RequestMapping("/api/orders")
@RequiredArgsConstructor
@Validated
public class OrderController {
    
    private final OrderService orderService;
    
    @PostMapping
    @ResponseStatus(HttpStatus.CREATED)
    public ResponseEntity<OrderResponse> createOrder(@Valid @RequestBody CreateOrderRequest request) {
        Order order = orderService.createOrder(request);
        return ResponseEntity.ok(OrderResponse.from(order));
    }
    
    @PutMapping("/{orderId}/transition")
    public ResponseEntity<OrderResponse> transitionOrder(
            @PathVariable Long orderId,
            @RequestParam OrderEvent event) {
        Order order = orderService.transitionOrderState(orderId, event);
        return ResponseEntity.ok(OrderResponse.from(order));
    }
    
    @GetMapping("/{orderId}")
    public ResponseEntity<OrderResponse> getOrder(@PathVariable Long orderId) {
        Order order = orderService.getOrderById(orderId);
        return ResponseEntity.ok(OrderResponse.from(order));
    }
}
```
