Now let me create a simple Nginx configuration file for the reverse proxy:


```properties
events {
    worker_connections 1024;
}

http {
    include       /etc/nginx/mime.types;
    default_type  application/octet-stream;

    # Logging
    log_format main '$remote_addr - $remote_user [$time_local] "$request" '
                    '$status $body_bytes_sent "$http_referer" '
                    '"$http_user_agent" "$http_x_forwarded_for"';

    access_log /var/log/nginx/access.log main;
    error_log /var/log/nginx/error.log warn;

    # Basic settings
    sendfile on;
    tcp_nopush on;
    tcp_nodelay on;
    keepalive_timeout 65;
    types_hash_max_size 2048;
    client_max_body_size 100M;

    # Gzip compression
    gzip on;
    gzip_vary on;
    gzip_min_length 1024;
    gzip_proxied any;
    gzip_comp_level 6;
    gzip_types
        text/plain
        text/css
        text/xml
        text/javascript
        application/json
        application/javascript
        application/xml+rss
        application/atom+xml
        image/svg+xml;

    # Rate limiting
    limit_req_zone $binary_remote_addr zone=api:10m rate=10r/s;
    limit_req_zone $binary_remote_addr zone=login:10m rate=5r/m;

    # Upstream backend servers
    upstream backend {
        server backend:8080;
        keepalive 32;
    }

    # HTTP server (redirect to HTTPS in production)
    server {
        listen 80;
        server_name _;
        
        # Health check endpoint
        location /health {
            access_log off;
            return 200 "healthy\n";
            add_header Content-Type text/plain;
        }

        # Redirect all other traffic to HTTPS in production
        location / {
            return 301 https://$host$request_uri;
        }
    }

    # HTTPS server
    server {
        listen 443 ssl http2;
        server_name _;

        # SSL configuration
        ssl_certificate /etc/nginx/ssl/cert.pem;
        ssl_certificate_key /etc/nginx/ssl/key.pem;
        ssl_protocols TLSv1.2 TLSv1.3;
        ssl_ciphers ECDHE-RSA-AES128-GCM-SHA256:ECDHE-RSA-AES256-GCM-SHA384:ECDHE-RSA-AES128-SHA256:ECDHE-RSA-AES256-SHA384;
        ssl_prefer_server_ciphers off;
        ssl_session_cache shared:SSL:10m;
        ssl_session_timeout 10m;

        # Security headers
        add_header X-Frame-Options DENY;
        add_header X-Content-Type-Options nosniff;
        add_header X-XSS-Protection "1; mode=block";
        add_header Strict-Transport-Security "max-age=31536000; includeSubDomains" always;

        # API endpoints with rate limiting
        location /api/ {
            limit_req zone=api burst=20 nodelay;
            proxy_pass http://backend;
            proxy_set_header Host $host;
            proxy_set_header X-Real-IP $remote_addr;
            proxy_set_header X-Forwarded-For $proxy_add_x_forwarded_for;
            proxy_set_header X-Forwarded-Proto $scheme;
            proxy_connect_timeout 30s;
            proxy_send_timeout 30s;
            proxy_read_timeout 30s;
        }

        # Actuator endpoints (health checks)
        location /actuator/ {
            proxy_pass http://backend;
            proxy_set_header Host $host;
            proxy_set_header X-Real-IP $remote_addr;
            proxy_set_header X-Forwarded-For $proxy_add_x_forwarded_for;
            proxy_set_header X-Forwarded-Proto $scheme;
        }

        # Static files
        location /static/ {
            proxy_pass http://backend;
            expires 1y;
            add_header Cache-Control "public, immutable";
        }

        # Default location
        location / {
            proxy_pass http://backend;
            proxy_set_header Host $host;
            proxy_set_header X-Real-IP $remote_addr;
            proxy_set_header X-Forwarded-For $proxy_add_x_forwarded_for;
            proxy_set_header X-Forwarded-Proto $scheme;
        }
    }
}
```

Now let me create a simple script to help with Docker operations:


```shellscript
#!/bin/bash

# Docker management script for ArtiCurated application
# Usage: ./docker-commands.sh [command]

set -e

# Colors for output
RED='\033[0;31m'
GREEN='\033[0;32m'
YELLOW='\033[1;33m'
BLUE='\033[0;34m'
NC='\033[0m' # No Color

# Function to print colored output
print_status() {
    echo -e "${BLUE}[INFO]${NC} $1"
}

print_success() {
    echo -e "${GREEN}[SUCCESS]${NC} $1"
}

print_warning() {
    echo -e "${YELLOW}[WARNING]${NC} $1"
}

print_error() {
    echo -e "${RED}[ERROR]${NC} $1"
}

# Function to check if Docker is running
check_docker() {
    if ! docker info > /dev/null 2>&1; then
        print_error "Docker is not running. Please start Docker and try again."
        exit 1
    fi
}

# Function to check if Docker Compose is available
check_docker_compose() {
    if ! command -v docker-compose > /dev/null 2>&1; then
        print_error "Docker Compose is not installed. Please install Docker Compose and try again."
        exit 1
    fi
}

# Function to build and start all services
start() {
    print_status "Starting ArtiCurated application..."
    check_docker
    check_docker_compose
    
    cd "$(dirname "$0")"
    
    print_status "Building and starting services..."
    docker-compose up -d --build
    
    print_success "Services started successfully!"
    print_status "Application will be available at: http://localhost:8080"
    print_status "PostgreSQL: localhost:5432"
    print_status "Redis: localhost:6379"
    
    # Wait for services to be healthy
    print_status "Waiting for services to be healthy..."
    sleep 10
    
    # Check service status
    status
}

# Function to stop all services
stop() {
    print_status "Stopping ArtiCurated application..."
    cd "$(dirname "$0")"
    docker-compose down
    print_success "Services stopped successfully!"
}

# Function to restart all services
restart() {
    print_status "Restarting ArtiCurated application..."
    stop
    start
}

# Function to show service status
status() {
    print_status "Checking service status..."
    cd "$(dirname "$0")"
    
    echo ""
    echo "Service Status:"
    echo "==============="
    docker-compose ps
    
    echo ""
    echo "Service Logs (last 10 lines):"
    echo "=============================="
    
    # Show logs for each service
    for service in backend postgres redis; do
        if docker-compose ps -q $service > /dev/null 2>&1; then
            echo ""
            echo "--- $service logs ---"
            docker-compose logs --tail=10 $service
        fi
    done
}

# Function to show logs for a specific service
logs() {
    local service=${1:-backend}
    print_status "Showing logs for $service service..."
    cd "$(dirname "$0")"
    docker-compose logs -f $service
}

# Function to execute command in a container
exec() {
    local service=${1:-backend}
    local command=${2:-/bin/bash}
    print_status "Executing command in $service container..."
    cd "$(dirname "$0")"
    docker-compose exec $service $command
}

# Function to clean up everything
cleanup() {
    print_warning "This will remove all containers, volumes, and images. Are you sure? (y/N)"
    read -r response
    if [[ "$response" =~ ^([yY][eE][sS]|[yY])$ ]]; then
        print_status "Cleaning up Docker resources..."
        cd "$(dirname "$0")"
        docker-compose down -v --rmi all
        docker system prune -f
        print_success "Cleanup completed!"
    else
        print_status "Cleanup cancelled."
    fi
}

# Function to show help
show_help() {
    echo "ArtiCurated Docker Management Script"
    echo "==================================="
    echo ""
    echo "Usage: $0 [command]"
    echo ""
    echo "Commands:"
    echo "  start     - Build and start all services"
    echo "  stop      - Stop all services"
    echo "  restart   - Restart all services"
    echo "  status    - Show service status and logs"
    echo "  logs      - Show logs for a service (default: backend)"
    echo "  exec      - Execute command in a container (default: backend)"
    echo "  cleanup   - Remove all containers, volumes, and images"
    echo "  help      - Show this help message"
    echo ""
    echo "Examples:"
    echo "  $0 start                    # Start all services"
    echo "  $0 logs postgres            # Show PostgreSQL logs"
    echo "  $0 exec backend /bin/bash   # Open bash in backend container"
    echo ""
}

# Main script logic
case "${1:-help}" in
    start)
        start
        ;;
    stop)
        stop
        ;;
    restart)
        restart
        ;;
    status)
        status
        ;;
    logs)
        logs "$2"
        ;;
    exec)
        exec "$2" "$3"
        ;;
    cleanup)
        cleanup
        ;;
    help|--help|-h)
        show_help
        ;;
    *)
        print_error "Unknown command: $1"
        show_help
        exit 1
        ;;
esac
```

Finally, let me create a README file for the Docker setup:


```markdown
# Docker Setup for ArtiCurated

This directory contains Docker configuration files for running the ArtiCurated Spring Boot application in containers.

## 🚀 Quick Start

### Prerequisites
- Docker Desktop installed and running
- Docker Compose installed
- At least 4GB of available RAM

### Start the Application
```bash
# Navigate to the docker directory
cd docker

# Start all services
./docker-commands.sh start

# Or use docker-compose directly
docker-compose up -d --build
```

### Stop the Application
```bash
./docker-commands.sh stop

# Or use docker-compose directly
docker-compose down
```

## 🏗️ Architecture

The application runs with the following services:

- **Backend**: Spring Boot application (port 8080)
- **PostgreSQL**: Database (port 5432)
- **Redis**: Caching and session management (port 6379)
- **Nginx**: Reverse proxy (ports 80, 443) - Production profile only

## 📁 Files

- **Dockerfile**: Multi-stage build for the Spring Boot application
- **docker-compose.yml**: Orchestrates all services
- **.dockerignore**: Excludes unnecessary files from build context
- **nginx/nginx.conf**: Nginx configuration for production
- **docker-commands.sh**: Helper script for common operations
- **README.md**: This documentation

## 🔧 Configuration

### Environment Variables

The application is configured through environment variables in `docker-compose.yml`:

#### Database
- `SPRING_DATASOURCE_URL`: PostgreSQL connection string
- `SPRING_DATASOURCE_USERNAME`: Database username
- `SPRING_DATASOURCE_PASSWORD`: Database password

#### Redis
- `SPRING_REDIS_HOST`: Redis host
- `SPRING_REDIS_PORT`: Redis port
- `SPRING_REDIS_PASSWORD`: Redis password

#### Application
- `SPRING_PROFILES_ACTIVE`: Active Spring profile (docker)
- `SERVER_PORT`: Application port
- `LOGGING_LEVEL_ROOT`: Root logging level

### Volumes

- `postgres_data`: Persistent PostgreSQL data
- `redis_data`: Persistent Redis data
- `app_logs`: Application logs

## 🚀 Usage

### Development Mode
```bash
# Start only essential services (no Nginx)
docker-compose up -d postgres redis backend
```

### Production Mode
```bash
# Start all services including Nginx
docker-compose --profile production up -d
```

### View Logs
```bash
# All services
docker-compose logs -f

# Specific service
docker-compose logs -f backend
./docker-commands.sh logs backend
```

### Execute Commands in Containers
```bash
# Open bash in backend container
./docker-commands.sh exec backend

# Execute specific command
./docker-commands.sh exec postgres psql -U articurated_user -d articurated
```

### Health Checks
```bash
# Check service status
./docker-commands.sh status

# Application health endpoint
curl http://localhost:8080/actuator/health
```

## 🛠️ Management Commands

The `docker-commands.sh` script provides convenient commands:

```bash
./docker-commands.sh start      # Start all services
./docker-commands.sh stop       # Stop all services
./docker-commands.sh restart    # Restart all services
./docker-commands.sh status     # Show service status
./docker-commands.sh logs       # Show logs
./docker-commands.sh exec       # Execute in container
./docker-commands.sh cleanup    # Remove all resources
./docker-commands.sh help       # Show help
```

## 🔍 Troubleshooting

### Common Issues

1. **Port conflicts**: Ensure ports 8080, 5432, and 6379 are available
2. **Memory issues**: Increase Docker Desktop memory allocation
3. **Permission errors**: Run `chmod +x docker-commands.sh`

### Debug Commands

```bash
# Check container status
docker-compose ps

# View detailed logs
docker-compose logs --tail=100 backend

# Check resource usage
docker stats

# Inspect container
docker-compose exec backend sh
```

### Reset Everything

```bash
# Remove all containers, volumes, and images
./docker-commands.sh cleanup

# Rebuild from scratch
docker-compose up -d --build --force-recreate
```

## 🔒 Security Notes

- Default passwords are set for development only
- Change passwords in production
- SSL certificates are required for Nginx in production
- Consider using Docker secrets for sensitive data

## 📊 Monitoring

### Health Endpoints
- Application: `http://localhost:8080/actuator/health`
- Nginx: `http://localhost/health` (production mode)

### Metrics
- Prometheus metrics: `http://localhost:8080/actuator/prometheus`
- Application info: `http://localhost:8080/actuator/info`

## 🚀 Production Deployment

For production deployment:

1. Set up SSL certificates in `nginx/ssl/`
2. Change default passwords
3. Use environment-specific configuration
4. Enable production profile: `docker-compose --profile production up -d`
5. Set up monitoring and logging
6. Configure backup strategies for volumes

## 📚 Additional Resources

- [Docker Compose documentation](https://docs.docker.com/compose/)
- [Spring Boot Docker guide](https://spring.io/guides/gs/spring-boot-docker/)
- [PostgreSQL Docker image](https://hub.docker.com/_/postgres)
- [Redis Docker image](https://hub.docker.com/_/redis)

## **📋 Application Configuration Features:**

### **🏗️ Multi-Profile Support:**

- **`docker`**: PostgreSQL + Redis configuration for Docker environment
- **`dev`**: Development profile with enhanced logging and H2 database
- **`prod`**: Production profile with environment variables and optimized settings

### **🗄️ Database Configuration:**
- **H2**: In-memory database for development/testing
- **PostgreSQL**: Production-ready database with connection pooling
- **HikariCP**: Optimized connection pool settings for each profile

### **🔴 Redis Configuration:**
- Connection pooling with Lettuce
- Profile-specific settings (local vs. Docker)
- Cache configuration with TTL settings

### **🔒 Security Configuration:**
- Basic authentication setup
- JWT configuration with customizable secrets
- Profile-specific security settings

### **📊 Monitoring & Management:**
- **Actuator**: Health checks, metrics, and Prometheus export
- **Logging**: Structured logging with file rotation
- **Metrics**: Performance monitoring and health endpoints

### **⚡ Performance Optimizations:**
- Connection pooling optimization
- Batch processing configuration
- Compression settings
- File upload limits

### **🌍 Environment Flexibility:**
- Environment variable support for production
- Profile-specific configurations
- Docker-compatible settings

## **🚀 Usage Examples:**

```

export DATABASE_PASSWORD=secure_password
./mvnw spring-boot:run -Dspring.profiles.active=prod
```

Now let me create a PostgreSQL initialization script for your Docker setup:


```sql
-- PostgreSQL initialization script for ArtiCurated application
-- This script will be executed when the PostgreSQL container starts

-- Create the main database if it doesn't exist
-- Note: PostgreSQL creates the database automatically from environment variables
-- but we can add additional setup here

-- Create extensions that might be useful
CREATE EXTENSION IF NOT EXISTS "uuid-ossp";
CREATE EXTENSION IF NOT EXISTS "pgcrypto";

-- Create additional schemas if needed
CREATE SCHEMA IF NOT EXISTS articurated;
CREATE SCHEMA IF NOT EXISTS audit;

-- Set search path
SET search_path TO articurated, public;

-- Create a function to update the updated_at timestamp
CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION update_updated_at_column()
RETURNS TRIGGER AS $$
BEGIN
    NEW.updated_at = CURRENT_TIMESTAMP;
    RETURN NEW;
END;
$$ language 'plpgsql';

-- Create audit logging function
CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION log_audit_event()
RETURNS TRIGGER AS $$
BEGIN
    IF TG_OP = 'INSERT' THEN
        INSERT INTO audit.audit_log (
            table_name, 
            operation, 
            record_id, 
            old_values, 
            new_values, 
            changed_by, 
            changed_at
        ) VALUES (
            TG_TABLE_NAME, 
            'INSERT', 
            NEW.id, 
            NULL, 
            to_jsonb(NEW), 
            COALESCE(NEW.created_by, 'system'), 
            CURRENT_TIMESTAMP
        );
        RETURN NEW;
    ELSIF TG_OP = 'UPDATE' THEN
        INSERT INTO audit.audit_log (
            table_name, 
            operation, 
            record_id, 
            old_values, 
            new_values, 
            changed_by, 
            changed_at
        ) VALUES (
            TG_TABLE_NAME, 
            'UPDATE', 
            NEW.id, 
            to_jsonb(OLD), 
            to_jsonb(NEW), 
            COALESCE(NEW.updated_by, 'system'), 
            CURRENT_TIMESTAMP
        );
        RETURN NEW;
    ELSIF TG_OP = 'DELETE' THEN
        INSERT INTO audit.audit_log (
            table_name, 
            operation, 
            record_id, 
            old_values, 
            new_values, 
            changed_by, 
            changed_at
        ) VALUES (
            TG_TABLE_NAME, 
            'DELETE', 
            OLD.id, 
            to_jsonb(OLD), 
            NULL, 
            COALESCE(OLD.deleted_by, 'system'), 
            CURRENT_TIMESTAMP
        );
        RETURN OLD;
    END IF;
    RETURN NULL;
END;
$$ language 'plpgsql';

-- Create audit log table
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS audit.audit_log (
    id BIGSERIAL PRIMARY KEY,
    table_name VARCHAR(100) NOT NULL,
    operation VARCHAR(20) NOT NULL,
    record_id BIGINT,
    old_values JSONB,
    new_values JSONB,
    changed_by VARCHAR(100),
    changed_at TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP
);

-- Create index on audit log for better performance
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_audit_log_table_name ON audit.audit_log(table_name);
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_audit_log_record_id ON audit.audit_log(record_id);
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_audit_log_changed_at ON audit.audit_log(changed_at);

-- Grant permissions to the application user
GRANT USAGE ON SCHEMA articurated TO articurated_user;
GRANT USAGE ON SCHEMA audit TO articurated_user;
GRANT ALL PRIVILEGES ON ALL TABLES IN SCHEMA articurated TO articurated_user;
GRANT ALL PRIVILEGES ON ALL TABLES IN SCHEMA audit TO articurated_user;
GRANT ALL PRIVILEGES ON ALL SEQUENCES IN SCHEMA articurated TO articurated_user;
GRANT ALL PRIVILEGES ON ALL SEQUENCES IN SCHEMA audit TO articurated_user;

-- Grant permissions on future tables
ALTER DEFAULT PRIVILEGES IN SCHEMA articurated GRANT ALL ON TABLES TO articurated_user;
ALTER DEFAULT PRIVILEGES IN SCHEMA articurated GRANT ALL ON SEQUENCES TO articurated_user;
ALTER DEFAULT PRIVILEGES IN SCHEMA audit GRANT ALL ON TABLES TO articurated_user;
ALTER DEFAULT PRIVILEGES IN SCHEMA audit GRANT ALL ON SEQUENCES TO articurated_user;

-- Create a function to get database version info
CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION get_database_info()
RETURNS TABLE (
    database_name TEXT,
    schema_name TEXT,
    table_count BIGINT,
    created_at TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE
) AS $$
BEGIN
    RETURN QUERY
    SELECT 
        current_database()::TEXT,
        s.schema_name::TEXT,
        COUNT(t.table_name)::BIGINT,
        CURRENT_TIMESTAMP
    FROM information_schema.schemata s
    LEFT JOIN information_schema.tables t ON s.schema_name = t.table_schema
    WHERE s.schema_name IN ('public', 'articurated', 'audit')
    GROUP BY s.schema_name
    ORDER BY s.schema_name;
END;
$$ LANGUAGE plpgsql;

-- Grant execute permission on the function
GRANT EXECUTE ON FUNCTION get_database_info() TO articurated_user;

-- Log the initialization
INSERT INTO audit.audit_log (
    table_name, 
    operation, 
    record_id, 
    old_values, 
    new_values, 
    changed_by, 
    changed_at
) VALUES (
    'database_init', 
    'INIT', 
    1, 
    NULL, 
    '{"message": "Database initialized successfully", "version": "1.0.0"}'::jsonb, 
    'system', 
    CURRENT_TIMESTAMP
);

-- Print success message
DO $$
BEGIN
    RAISE NOTICE 'ArtiCurated database initialized successfully!';
    RAISE NOTICE 'Database: %', current_database();
    RAISE NOTICE 'User: %', current_user;
    RAISE NOTICE 'Schema: %', current_schema;
END $$;
```

Now let me create a local PostgreSQL setup script for development:


```shellscript
#!/bin/bash

# PostgreSQL Setup Script for ArtiCurated Application
# This script helps set up PostgreSQL locally for development

set -e

# Colors for output
RED='\033[0;31m'
GREEN='\033[0;32m'
YELLOW='\033[1;33m'
BLUE='\033[0;34m'
NC='\033[0m' # No Color

# Configuration
DB_NAME="articurated"
DB_USER="articurated_user"
DB_PASSWORD="articurated_password"
DB_HOST="localhost"
DB_PORT="5432"

# Function to print colored output
print_status() {
    echo -e "${BLUE}[INFO]${NC} $1"
}

print_success() {
    echo -e "${GREEN}[SUCCESS]${NC} $1"
}

print_warning() {
    echo -e "${YELLOW}[WARNING]${NC} $1"
}

print_error() {
    echo -e "${RED}[ERROR]${NC} $1"
}

# Function to check if PostgreSQL is installed
check_postgresql() {
    if ! command -v psql > /dev/null 2>&1; then
        print_error "PostgreSQL client (psql) is not installed."
        print_status "Please install PostgreSQL first:"
        echo ""
        echo "Ubuntu/Debian: sudo apt-get install postgresql postgresql-contrib"
        echo "CentOS/RHEL: sudo yum install postgresql postgresql-contrib"
        echo "macOS: brew install postgresql"
        echo "Windows: Download from https://www.postgresql.org/download/windows/"
        echo ""
        exit 1
    fi
    
    if ! command -v createdb > /dev/null 2>&1; then
        print_error "PostgreSQL utilities are not installed."
        print_status "Please install PostgreSQL server and utilities."
        exit 1
    fi
}

# Function to check if PostgreSQL service is running
check_postgresql_service() {
    if ! pg_isready -h $DB_HOST -p $DB_PORT > /dev/null 2>&1; then
        print_error "PostgreSQL service is not running on $DB_HOST:$DB_PORT"
        print_status "Please start PostgreSQL service:"
        echo ""
        echo "Ubuntu/Debian: sudo systemctl start postgresql"
        echo "CentOS/RHEL: sudo systemctl start postgresql"
        echo "macOS: brew services start postgresql"
        echo "Windows: Start PostgreSQL service from Services"
        echo ""
        exit 1
    fi
}

# Function to create database and user
setup_database() {
    print_status "Setting up PostgreSQL database..."
    
    # Create user if it doesn't exist
    if ! psql -h $DB_HOST -p $DB_PORT -U postgres -lqt | cut -d \| -f 1 | grep -qw $DB_USER; then
        print_status "Creating user: $DB_USER"
        createuser -h $DB_HOST -p $DB_PORT -U postgres --createdb --login --pwprompt $DB_USER
    else
        print_status "User $DB_USER already exists"
    fi
    
    # Create database if it doesn't exist
    if ! psql -h $DB_HOST -p $DB_PORT -U postgres -lqt | cut -d \| -f 1 | grep -qw $DB_NAME; then
        print_status "Creating database: $DB_NAME"
        createdb -h $DB_HOST -p $DB_PORT -U postgres -O $DB_USER $DB_NAME
    else
        print_status "Database $DB_NAME already exists"
    fi
    
    # Test connection
    if psql -h $DB_HOST -p $DB_PORT -U $DB_USER -d $DB_NAME -c "SELECT version();" > /dev/null 2>&1; then
        print_success "Database connection successful!"
    else
        print_error "Failed to connect to database"
        exit 1
    fi
}

# Function to run initialization script
run_init_script() {
    print_status "Running database initialization script..."
    
    if [ -f "docker/init-scripts/01-init-database.sql" ]; then
        psql -h $DB_HOST -p $DB_PORT -U $DB_USER -d $DB_NAME -f docker/init-scripts/01-init-database.sql
        print_success "Database initialization completed!"
    else
        print_warning "Initialization script not found. Skipping..."
    fi
}

# Function to show connection info
show_connection_info() {
    echo ""
    echo "=========================================="
    echo "PostgreSQL Connection Information"
    echo "=========================================="
    echo "Host: $DB_HOST"
    echo "Port: $DB_PORT"
    echo "Database: $DB_NAME"
    echo "Username: $DB_USER"
    echo "Password: $DB_PASSWORD"
    echo ""
    echo "Connection String:"
    echo "jdbc:postgresql://$DB_HOST:$DB_PORT/$DB_NAME"
    echo ""
    echo "Test Connection:"
    echo "psql -h $DB_HOST -p $DB_PORT -U $DB_USER -d $DB_NAME"
    echo ""
}

# Function to show help
show_help() {
    echo "PostgreSQL Setup Script for ArtiCurated"
    echo "======================================="
    echo ""
    echo "Usage: $0 [option]"
    echo ""
    echo "Options:"
    echo "  setup     - Set up database and user (default)"
    echo "  test      - Test database connection"
    echo "  info      - Show connection information"
    echo "  help      - Show this help message"
    echo ""
    echo "Examples:"
    echo "  $0 setup     # Set up database and user"
    echo "  $0 test      # Test connection"
    echo "  $0 info      # Show connection info"
    echo ""
}

# Function to test connection
test_connection() {
    print_status "Testing database connection..."
    
    if psql -h $DB_HOST -p $DB_PORT -U $DB_USER -d $DB_NAME -c "SELECT version();" > /dev/null 2>&1; then
        print_success "Database connection successful!"
        psql -h $DB_HOST -p $DB_PORT -U $DB_USER -d $DB_NAME -c "SELECT version();"
    else
        print_error "Database connection failed!"
        exit 1
    fi
}

# Main script logic
case "${1:-setup}" in
    setup)
        check_postgresql
        check_postgresql_service
        setup_database
        run_init_script
        show_connection_info
        print_success "PostgreSQL setup completed successfully!"
        ;;
    test)
        check_postgresql
        test_connection
        ;;
    info)
        show_connection_info
        ;;
    help|--help|-h)
        show_help
        ;;
    *)
        print_error "Unknown option: $1"
        show_help
        exit 1
        ;;
esac
```

Now let me create a Windows PowerShell version of the setup script:


```powershell
# PostgreSQL Setup Script for ArtiCurated Application (Windows PowerShell)
# This script helps set up PostgreSQL locally for development on Windows

param(
    [string]$Action = "setup"
)

# Configuration
$DB_NAME = "articurated"
$DB_USER = "articurated_user"
$DB_PASSWORD = "articurated_password"
$DB_HOST = "localhost"
$DB_PORT = "5432"

# Function to print colored output
function Write-Status {
    param([string]$Message)
    Write-Host "[INFO] $Message" -ForegroundColor Blue
}

function Write-Success {
    param([string]$Message)
    Write-Host "[SUCCESS] $Message" -ForegroundColor Green
}

function Write-Warning {
    param([string]$Message)
    Write-Host "[WARNING] $Message" -ForegroundColor Yellow
}

function Write-Error {
    param([string]$Message)
    Write-Host "[ERROR] $Message" -ForegroundColor Red
}

# Function to check if PostgreSQL is installed
function Test-PostgreSQLInstalled {
    try {
        $psqlPath = Get-Command psql -ErrorAction Stop
        Write-Status "PostgreSQL client found at: $($psqlPath.Source)"
        return $true
    }
    catch {
        Write-Error "PostgreSQL client (psql) is not installed or not in PATH."
        Write-Status "Please install PostgreSQL first:"
        Write-Host ""
        Write-Host "1. Download from: https://www.postgresql.org/download/windows/"
        Write-Host "2. Run the installer and add PostgreSQL to PATH"
        Write-Host "3. Restart PowerShell after installation"
        Write-Host ""
        return $false
    }
}

# Function to check if PostgreSQL service is running
function Test-PostgreSQLService {
    try {
        $service = Get-Service -Name "*postgresql*" -ErrorAction Stop
        if ($service.Status -eq "Running") {
            Write-Status "PostgreSQL service is running"
            return $true
        }
        else {
            Write-Warning "PostgreSQL service is not running. Attempting to start..."
            Start-Service $service
            Start-Sleep -Seconds 5
            if ((Get-Service $service).Status -eq "Running") {
                Write-Success "PostgreSQL service started successfully"
                return $true
            }
            else {
                Write-Error "Failed to start PostgreSQL service"
                return $false
            }
        }
    }
    catch {
        Write-Error "PostgreSQL service not found. Please ensure PostgreSQL is properly installed."
        return $false
    }
}

# Function to test database connection
function Test-DatabaseConnection {
    try {
        $env:PGPASSWORD = $DB_PASSWORD
        $result = psql -h $DB_HOST -p $DB_PORT -U $DB_USER -d $DB_NAME -c "SELECT version();" 2>$null
        if ($LASTEXITCODE -eq 0) {
            Write-Success "Database connection successful!"
            return $true
        }
        else {
            Write-Error "Database connection failed!"
            return $false
        }
    }
    catch {
        Write-Error "Database connection failed: $($_.Exception.Message)"
        return $false
    }
    finally {
        Remove-Item Env:PGPASSWORD -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
    }
}

# Function to create database and user
function Setup-Database {
    Write-Status "Setting up PostgreSQL database..."
    
    try {
        $env:PGPASSWORD = "postgres"  # Default postgres user password
        
        # Create user if it doesn't exist
        Write-Status "Creating user: $DB_USER"
        $createUserResult = psql -h $DB_HOST -p $DB_PORT -U postgres -c "CREATE USER $DB_USER WITH PASSWORD '$DB_PASSWORD' CREATEDB LOGIN;" 2>$null
        if ($LASTEXITCODE -eq 0) {
            Write-Success "User $DB_USER created successfully"
        }
        else {
            Write-Warning "User $DB_USER might already exist or creation failed"
        }
        
        # Create database if it doesn't exist
        Write-Status "Creating database: $DB_NAME"
        $createDbResult = psql -h $DB_HOST -p $DB_PORT -U postgres -c "CREATE DATABASE $DB_NAME OWNER $DB_USER;" 2>$null
        if ($LASTEXITCODE -eq 0) {
            Write-Success "Database $DB_NAME created successfully"
        }
        else {
            Write-Warning "Database $DB_NAME might already exist or creation failed"
        }
        
        # Test connection with new user
        if (Test-DatabaseConnection) {
            Write-Success "Database setup completed successfully!"
        }
        else {
            Write-Error "Database setup failed!"
            return $false
        }
    }
    catch {
        Write-Error "Database setup failed: $($_.Exception.Message)"
        return $false
    }
    finally {
        Remove-Item Env:PGPASSWORD -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
    }
    
    return $true
}

# Function to run initialization script
function Run-InitScript {
    Write-Status "Running database initialization script..."
    
    $initScriptPath = "docker\init-scripts\01-init-database.sql"
    if (Test-Path $initScriptPath) {
        try {
            $env:PGPASSWORD = $DB_PASSWORD
            $result = psql -h $DB_HOST -p $DB_PORT -U $DB_USER -d $DB_NAME -f $initScriptPath
            if ($LASTEXITCODE -eq 0) {
                Write-Success "Database initialization completed!"
                return $true
            }
            else {
                Write-Error "Database initialization failed!"
                return $false
            }
        }
        catch {
            Write-Error "Database initialization failed: $($_.Exception.Message)"
            return $false
        }
        finally {
            Remove-Item Env:PGPASSWORD -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
        }
    }
    else {
        Write-Warning "Initialization script not found at: $initScriptPath"
        Write-Warning "Skipping initialization..."
        return $true
    }
}

# Function to show connection info
function Show-ConnectionInfo {
    Write-Host ""
    Write-Host "==========================================" -ForegroundColor Cyan
    Write-Host "PostgreSQL Connection Information" -ForegroundColor Cyan
    Write-Host "==========================================" -ForegroundColor Cyan
    Write-Host "Host: $DB_HOST"
    Write-Host "Port: $DB_PORT"
    Write-Host "Database: $DB_NAME"
    Write-Host "Username: $DB_USER"
    Write-Host "Password: $DB_PASSWORD"
    Write-Host ""
    Write-Host "Connection String:" -ForegroundColor Yellow
    Write-Host "jdbc:postgresql://$DB_HOST`:$DB_PORT/$DB_NAME"
    Write-Host ""
    Write-Host "Test Connection:" -ForegroundColor Yellow
    Write-Host "psql -h $DB_HOST -p $DB_PORT -U $DB_USER -d $DB_NAME"
    Write-Host ""
}

# Function to show help
function Show-Help {
    Write-Host "PostgreSQL Setup Script for ArtiCurated (Windows)" -ForegroundColor Cyan
    Write-Host "=================================================" -ForegroundColor Cyan
    Write-Host ""
    Write-Host "Usage: .\setup-postgresql.ps1 [option]" -ForegroundColor Yellow
    Write-Host ""
    Write-Host "Options:" -ForegroundColor Yellow
    Write-Host "  setup     - Set up database and user (default)"
    Write-Host "  test      - Test database connection"
    Write-Host "  info      - Show connection information"
    Write-Host "  help      - Show this help message"
    Write-Host ""
    Write-Host "Examples:" -ForegroundColor Yellow
    Write-Host "  .\setup-postgresql.ps1 setup     # Set up database and user"
    Write-Host "  .\setup-postgresql.ps1 test      # Test connection"
    Write-Host "  .\setup-postgresql.ps1 info      # Show connection info"
    Write-Host ""
}

# Main script logic
switch ($Action.ToLower()) {
    "setup" {
        if (-not (Test-PostgreSQLInstalled)) {
            exit 1
        }
        if (-not (Test-PostgreSQLService)) {
            exit 1
        }
        if (Setup-Database) {
            Run-InitScript
            Show-ConnectionInfo
            Write-Success "PostgreSQL setup completed successfully!"
        }
        else {
            Write-Error "PostgreSQL setup failed!"
            exit 1
        }
    }
    "test" {
        if (-not (Test-PostgreSQLInstalled)) {
            exit 1
        }
        if (Test-DatabaseConnection) {
            Write-Success "Database connection test passed!"
        }
        else {
            Write-Error "Database connection test failed!"
            exit 1
        }
    }
    "info" {
        Show-ConnectionInfo
    }
    "help" {
        Show-Help
    }
    default {
        Write-Error "Unknown option: $Action"
        Show-Help
        exit 1
    }
}
```

Now let me create a README file specifically for PostgreSQL setup:


```markdown
# PostgreSQL Setup Guide for ArtiCurated

This guide will help you set up PostgreSQL for your ArtiCurated Spring Boot application, both locally and in Docker.

## 🚀 Quick Start

### Option 1: Docker (Recommended for Development)
```bash
# Navigate to docker directory
cd docker

# Start PostgreSQL with Docker Compose
docker-compose up -d postgres

# The database will be automatically created with:
# - Database: articurated
# - Username: articurated_user
# - Password: articurated_password
# - Port: 5432
```

### Option 2: Local PostgreSQL Installation
```bash
# Windows (PowerShell)
.\scripts\setup-postgresql.ps1 setup

# Linux/macOS
./scripts/setup-postgresql.sh setup
```

## 📋 Prerequisites

### For Docker Setup
- Docker Desktop installed and running
- Docker Compose installed

### For Local Setup
- PostgreSQL 12+ installed
- PostgreSQL service running
- `psql` command-line tool available in PATH

## 🐳 Docker Setup (Recommended)

### 1. Start PostgreSQL Container
```bash
cd docker
docker-compose up -d postgres
```

### 2. Verify Container Status
```bash
docker-compose ps postgres
```

### 3. Check Logs
```bash
docker-compose logs postgres
```

### 4. Connect to Database
```bash
# Connect using Docker
docker-compose exec postgres psql -U articurated_user -d articurated

# Or connect from host machine
psql -h localhost -p 5432 -U articurated_user -d articurated
```

## 💻 Local PostgreSQL Setup

### Windows Installation

1. **Download PostgreSQL**
   - Visit: https://www.postgresql.org/download/windows/
   - Download the latest version for Windows

2. **Install PostgreSQL**
   - Run the installer
   - Choose installation directory
   - Set password for `postgres` user
   - **Important**: Check "Add PostgreSQL to PATH"

3. **Setup Database**
   ```powershell
   # Run PowerShell as Administrator
   .\scripts\setup-postgresql.ps1 setup
   ```

### Linux Installation

#### Ubuntu/Debian
```bash
sudo apt update
sudo apt install postgresql postgresql-contrib
sudo systemctl start postgresql
sudo systemctl enable postgresql
```

#### CentOS/RHEL
```bash
sudo yum install postgresql postgresql-contrib
sudo systemctl start postgresql
sudo systemctl enable postgresql
```

#### Setup Database
```bash
chmod +x scripts/setup-postgresql.sh
./scripts/setup-postgresql.sh setup
```

### macOS Installation

```bash
# Using Homebrew
brew install postgresql
brew services start postgresql

# Setup Database
chmod +x scripts/setup-postgresql.sh
./scripts/setup-postgresql.sh setup
```

## 🔧 Configuration

### Application Configuration

Your `application.yml` is already configured for PostgreSQL:

```yaml
spring:
  datasource:
    url: jdbc:postgresql://localhost:5432/articurated
    driver-class-name: org.postgresql.Driver
    username: articurated_user
    password: articurated_password
```

### Environment Variables

You can override database settings using environment variables:

```bash
export SPRING_DATASOURCE_URL=jdbc:postgresql://localhost:5432/articurated
export SPRING_DATASOURCE_USERNAME=articurated_user
export SPRING_DATASOURCE_PASSWORD=articurated_password
```

## 🗄️ Database Schema

The application will automatically create tables based on your JPA entities. The initialization script (`docker/init-scripts/01-init-database.sql`) provides:

- **Extensions**: `uuid-ossp`, `pgcrypto`
- **Schemas**: `articurated`, `audit`
- **Audit Functions**: Automatic audit logging
- **Utility Functions**: Database information helpers

## 🔍 Testing Connection

### Test Database Connection
```bash
# Windows
.\scripts\setup-postgresql.ps1 test

# Linux/macOS
./scripts/setup-postgresql.sh test
```

### Manual Connection Test
```bash
psql -h localhost -p 5432 -U articurated_user -d articurated -c "SELECT version();"
```

### Test from Application
```bash
# Start your Spring Boot application
./mvnw spring-boot:run

# Check health endpoint
curl http://localhost:8080/actuator/health
```

## 🚨 Troubleshooting

### Common Issues

#### 1. Connection Refused
```bash
# Check if PostgreSQL is running
# Windows
Get-Service "*postgresql*"

# Linux/macOS
sudo systemctl status postgresql
```

#### 2. Authentication Failed
```bash
# Check pg_hba.conf for authentication settings
# Default location: /etc/postgresql/{version}/main/pg_hba.conf
```

#### 3. Port Already in Use
```bash
# Check what's using port 5432
netstat -an | grep 5432

# Change port in application.yml if needed
spring:
  datasource:
    url: jdbc:postgresql://localhost:5433/articurated
```

#### 4. Permission Denied
```bash
# Ensure user has proper permissions
sudo -u postgres psql -c "GRANT ALL PRIVILEGES ON DATABASE articurated TO articurated_user;"
```

### Reset Database

#### Docker Reset
```bash
cd docker
docker-compose down -v
docker-compose up -d postgres
```

#### Local Reset
```bash
# Drop and recreate database
dropdb -h localhost -U postgres articurated
createdb -h localhost -U postgres -O articurated_user articurated
```

## 📊 Monitoring

### Database Statistics
```sql
-- Connect to database
psql -h localhost -U articurated_user -d articurated

-- View database size
SELECT pg_size_pretty(pg_database_size('articurated'));

-- View table sizes
SELECT 
    schemaname,
    tablename,
    pg_size_pretty(pg_total_relation_size(schemaname||'.'||tablename)) as size
FROM pg_tables 
WHERE schemaname = 'articurated'
ORDER BY pg_total_relation_size(schemaname||'.'||tablename) DESC;
```

### Application Health
```bash
# Health check endpoint
curl http://localhost:8080/actuator/health

# Database health
curl http://localhost:8080/actuator/health/db
```

## 🔒 Security Considerations

### Production Security
1. **Change Default Passwords**
2. **Use Environment Variables**
3. **Enable SSL Connections**
4. **Restrict Network Access**
5. **Regular Security Updates**

### Example Production Configuration
```yaml
spring:
  datasource:
    url: jdbc:postgresql://${DB_HOST}:${DB_PORT}/${DB_NAME}?sslmode=require
    username: ${DB_USERNAME}
    password: ${DB_PASSWORD}
```

## 📚 Additional Resources

- [PostgreSQL Official Documentation](https://www.postgresql.org/docs/)
- [Spring Boot Data JPA](https://spring.io/guides/gs/accessing-data-jpa/)
- [Hibernate Documentation](https://hibernate.org/orm/documentation/)
- [Docker PostgreSQL Image](https://hub.docker.com/_/postgres)

## 🆘 Getting Help

If you encounter issues:

1. Check the logs: `docker-compose logs postgres`
2. Verify connection: `psql -h localhost -p 5432 -U articurated_user -d articurated`
3. Check application logs for Spring Boot errors
4. Ensure all services are running and accessible

## 🎯 Next Steps

After setting up PostgreSQL:

1. **Start your application**: `./mvnw spring-boot:run`
2. **Verify database connection** in application logs
3. **Create your JPA entities** in the `model` package
4. **Implement repositories** in the `repository` package
5. **Test CRUD operations** through your application

```dockercompose
version: '3.8'

services:
  # PostgreSQL Database
  postgres:
    image: postgres:15-alpine
    container_name: articurated-postgres
    environment:
      POSTGRES_DB: articurated
      POSTGRES_USER: articurated_user
      POSTGRES_PASSWORD: articurated_password
      POSTGRES_INITDB_ARGS: "--encoding=UTF-8 --lc-collate=C --lc-ctype=C"
    volumes:
      - postgres_data:/var/lib/postgresql/data
      - ./init-scripts:/docker-entrypoint-initdb.d
    ports:
      - "5432:5432"
    networks:
      - articurated-network
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD-SHELL", "pg_isready -U articurated_user -d articurated"]
      interval: 30s
      timeout: 10s
      retries: 3
      start_period: 40s
    restart: unless-stopped

  # Redis for caching and session management
  redis:
    image: redis:7-alpine
    container_name: articurated-redis
    command: redis-server --appendonly yes --requirepass redis_password
    volumes:
      - redis_data:/data
    ports:
      - "6379:6379"
    networks:
      - articurated-network
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD", "redis-cli", "--raw", "incr", "ping"]
      interval: 30s
      timeout: 10s
      retries: 3
      start_period: 30s
    restart: unless-stopped

  # Spring Boot Application
  backend:
    build:
      context: ..
      dockerfile: docker/Dockerfile
    container_name: articurated-backend
    environment:
      # Database configuration
      SPRING_DATASOURCE_URL: jdbc:postgresql://postgres:5432/articurated
      SPRING_DATASOURCE_USERNAME: articurated_user
      SPRING_DATASOURCE_PASSWORD: articurated_password
      SPRING_DATASOURCE_DRIVER_CLASS_NAME: org.postgresql.Driver
      
      # JPA/Hibernate configuration
      SPRING_JPA_HIBERNATE_DDL_AUTO: update
      SPRING_JPA_SHOW_SQL: false
      SPRING_JPA_PROPERTIES_HIBERNATE_DIALECT: org.hibernate.dialect.PostgreSQLDialect
      SPRING_JPA_PROPERTIES_HIBERNATE_FORMAT_SQL: true
      
      # Redis configuration
      SPRING_REDIS_HOST: redis
      SPRING_REDIS_PORT: 6379
      SPRING_REDIS_PASSWORD: redis_password
      
      # Application configuration
      SPRING_PROFILES_ACTIVE: docker
      SERVER_PORT: 8080
      
      # Logging
      LOGGING_LEVEL_ROOT: INFO
      LOGGING_LEVEL_COM_ARTICURATED: DEBUG
      
      # Security (for development - change in production)
      SPRING_SECURITY_USER_NAME: admin
      SPRING_SECURITY_USER_PASSWORD: admin123
      
      # Actuator
      MANAGEMENT_ENDPOINTS_WEB_EXPOSURE_INCLUDE: health,info,metrics,prometheus
      MANAGEMENT_ENDPOINT_HEALTH_SHOW-DETAILS: always
      
      # Batch configuration
      SPRING_BATCH_JOB_ENABLED: false
      SPRING_BATCH_JOB_NAMES: 
      
      # Integration configuration
      SPRING_INTEGRATION_HTTP_ENABLED: true
      
    ports:
      - "8080:8080"
    networks:
      - articurated-network
    depends_on:
      postgres:
        condition: service_healthy
      redis:
        condition: service_healthy
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD", "wget", "--no-verbose", "--tries=1", "--spider", "http://localhost:8080/actuator/health"]
      interval: 30s
      timeout: 10s
      retries: 3
      start_period: 60s
    restart: unless-stopped
    volumes:
      - app_logs:/app/logs

  # Nginx reverse proxy (optional)
  nginx:
    image: nginx:alpine
    container_name: articurated-nginx
    ports:
      - "80:80"
      - "443:443"
    volumes:
      - ./nginx/nginx.conf:/etc/nginx/nginx.conf:ro
      - ./nginx/ssl:/etc/nginx/ssl:ro
    networks:
      - articurated-network
    depends_on:
      - backend
    restart: unless-stopped
    profiles:
      - production

volumes:
  postgres_data:
    driver: local
  redis_data:
    driver: local
  app_logs:
    driver: local

networks:
  articurated-network:
    driver: bridge
    ipam:
      config:
        - subnet: 172.20.0.0/16

```dockerfile
# Multi-stage build for Spring Boot application
FROM eclipse-temurin:17-jdk-alpine AS builder

# Set working directory
WORKDIR /app

# Copy Maven wrapper and pom.xml first for better layer caching
COPY mvnw .
COPY .mvn .mvn
COPY pom.xml .

# Make mvnw executable
RUN chmod +x mvnw

# Download dependencies (this layer will be cached if pom.xml doesn't change)
RUN ./mvnw dependency:go-offline -B

# Copy source code
COPY src src

# Build the application
RUN ./mvnw clean package -DskipTests

# Runtime stage
FROM eclipse-temurin:17-jre-alpine

# Create app user for security
RUN addgroup -g 1001 -S appgroup && \
    adduser -u 1001 -S appuser -G appgroup

# Set working directory
WORKDIR /app

# Copy the built JAR from builder stage
COPY --from=builder /app/target/*.jar app.jar

# Change ownership to app user
RUN chown appuser:appgroup app.jar

# Switch to non-root user
USER appuser

# Expose port
EXPOSE 8080

# Health check
HEALTHCHECK --interval=30s --timeout=3s --start-period=60s --retries=3 \
    CMD wget --no-verbose --tries=1 --spider http://localhost:8080/actuator/health || exit 1

# Set JVM options for containerized environment
ENV JAVA_OPTS="-Xms512m -Xmx1024m -XX:+UseG1GC -XX:+UseContainerSupport"

# Run the application
ENTRYPOINT ["sh", "-c", "java $JAVA_OPTS -jar app.jar"]

ENTRYPOINT ["java", "-jar", "app.jar"]

# Docker Setup for ArtiCurated Skeleton

Simple Docker configuration for your Spring Boot skeleton project.

## 🚀 Quick Start

### 1. Build the Application
```bash
# From project root
./mvnw clean package
```

### 2. Start PostgreSQL
```bash
cd docker
docker-compose up -d postgres
```

### 3. Run the Application
```bash
# From project root
./mvnw spring-boot:run
```

## 📁 Files

- **`Dockerfile`** - Simple container for Spring Boot app
- **`docker-compose.yml`** - PostgreSQL database only
- **`.dockerignore`** - Optimized build context

## 🔧 Usage

### Start Database
```bash
cd docker
docker-compose up -d
```

### Stop Database
```bash
cd docker
docker-compose down
```

### View Logs
```bash
docker-compose logs postgres
```

## 🌐 Connection Details

- **Database**: PostgreSQL
- **Host**: localhost
- **Port**: 5432
- **Database**: articurated
- **Username**: articurated_user
- **Password**: articurated_password

## 📝 Notes

- This is a minimal setup for skeleton development
- PostgreSQL data is persisted in Docker volume
- Application runs locally, not in Docker (for simplicity)
- Add more services as your project grows

### **Order Domain - Core Entity**


```java
package com.articurated.order.domain;

import jakarta.persistence.*;
import lombok.Data;
import lombok.NoArgsConstructor;
import lombok.AllArgsConstructor;
import lombok.Builder;
import org.springframework.data.annotation.CreatedDate;
import org.springframework.data.annotation.LastModifiedDate;
import org.springframework.data.jpa.domain.support.AuditingEntityListener;

import java.math.BigDecimal;
import java.time.LocalDateTime;
import java.util.ArrayList;
import java.util.List;

@Entity
@Table(name = "orders")
@Data
@NoArgsConstructor
@AllArgsConstructor
@Builder
@EntityListeners(AuditingEntityListener.class)
public class Order {
    
    @Id
    @GeneratedValue(strategy = GenerationType.IDENTITY)
    private Long id;
    
    @Column(nullable = false, unique = true)
    private String orderNumber;
    
    @Column(nullable = false)
    @Enumerated(EnumType.STRING)
    private OrderState state;
    
    @Column(nullable = false)
    private String customerId;
    
    @Column(nullable = false)
    private String customerName;
    
    @Column(nullable = false)
    private String customerEmail;
    
    @Column(nullable = false)
    private BigDecimal totalAmount;
    
    @Column(nullable = false)
    private String currency;
    
    @Column(length = 1000)
    private String notes;
    
    @OneToMany(mappedBy = "order", cascade = CascadeType.ALL, fetch = FetchType.LAZY)
    private List<OrderStateHistory> stateHistory = new ArrayList<>();
    
    @CreatedDate
    @Column(nullable = false, updatable = false)
    private LocalDateTime createdAt;
    
    @LastModifiedDate
    @Column(nullable = false)
    private LocalDateTime updatedAt;
    
    @PrePersist
    protected void onCreate() {
        createdAt = LocalDateTime.now();
        updatedAt = LocalDateTime.now();
        if (state == null) {
            state = OrderState.CREATED;
        }
    }
    
    @PreUpdate
    protected void onUpdate() {
        updatedAt = LocalDateTime.now();
    }
    
    // Domain methods
    public void transitionTo(OrderState newState) {
        if (this.state.canTransitionTo(newState)) {
            OrderState oldState = this.state;
            this.state = newState;
            
            // Add to state history
            OrderStateHistory history = OrderStateHistory.builder()
                .order(this)
                .fromState(oldState)
                .toState(newState)
                .transitionTime(LocalDateTime.now())
                .build();
            
            this.stateHistory.add(history);
        } else {
            throw new IllegalStateException(
                String.format("Cannot transition from %s to %s", this.state, newState)
            );
        }
    }
    
    public boolean canTransitionTo(OrderState newState) {
        return this.state.canTransitionTo(newState);
    }
    
    public boolean isInFinalState() {
        return this.state.isFinal();
    }
}
```

### **Order State Enum**


```java
package com.articurated.order.domain;

import java.util.Set;

public enum OrderState {
    
    CREATED(Set.of(), false),
    PENDING_PAYMENT(Set.of(CREATED), false),
    PAID(Set.of(PENDING_PAYMENT), false),
    PROCESSING(Set.of(PAID), false),
    SHIPPED(Set.of(PROCESSING), false),
    DELIVERED(Set.of(SHIPPED), false),
    CANCELLED(Set.of(CREATED, PENDING_PAYMENT), true),
    REFUNDED(Set.of(PAID, PROCESSING, SHIPPED, DELIVERED), true);
    
    private final Set<OrderState> allowedTransitions;
    private final boolean isFinal;
    
    OrderState(Set<OrderState> allowedTransitions, boolean isFinal) {
        this.allowedTransitions = allowedTransitions;
        this.isFinal = isFinal;
    }
    
    public boolean canTransitionTo(OrderState newState) {
        return allowedTransitions.contains(newState);
    }
    
    public boolean isFinal() {
        return isFinal;
    }
    
    public Set<OrderState> getAllowedTransitions() {
        return allowedTransitions;
    }
}
```

public class OrderStateHistory {

    private Long id;
    
    @ManyToOne(fetch = FetchType.LAZY)
    @JoinColumn(name = "order_id", nullable = false)

    @Column(nullable = false)
    @Enumerated(EnumType.STRING)
    private OrderState fromState;
    
    @Column(nullable = false)
    @Enumerated(EnumType.STRING)
    private OrderState toState;
    
    @Column(nullable = false)
    private LocalDateTime transitionTime;
    
    @Column(length = 500)
    private String notes;
    
    @CreatedDate
    @Column(nullable = false, updatable = false)
    private LocalDateTime createdAt;
    
    @PrePersist
    protected void onCreate() {
        createdAt = LocalDateTime.now();
    }
}

Based on the current project structure we've created, this is called a **Domain-Driven Design (DDD) Architecture** or **Domain-Driven Design Pattern**. 

## **🏗️ Current Project Structure: Domain-Driven Design (DDD)**

### **📚 What is Domain-Driven Design?**

Domain-Driven Design is a software development approach that:
- **Focuses on the core business domain** and its logic
- **Organizes code around business concepts** rather than technical concerns
- **Uses ubiquitous language** that both developers and business experts understand
- **Separates concerns** into distinct bounded contexts

### **🎯 Key Characteristics of Your Current Structure:**

1. **📁 Domain-Centric Organization**
   - `order/` - Order management domain
   - `returns/` - Returns processing domain
   - `messaging/` - Asynchronous communication domain

2. **🏛️ Layered Architecture Within Each Domain**
   ```
   domain/     → Business entities and logic
   repository/ → Data access layer
   service/    → Business operations
   controller/ → API endpoints
   dto/        → Data transfer objects
   statemachine/ → Workflow management
   ```

3. **🔄 Shared Infrastructure**
   - `shared/config/` - Cross-cutting configurations
   - `shared/exception/` - Global error handling
   - `shared/events/` - Domain events

4. **⚡ Event-Driven Architecture**
   - Message producers and consumers
   - Asynchronous processing
   - Domain events for loose coupling

### **🔍 Alternative Names for This Pattern:**

- **Domain-Driven Design (DDD)**
- **Hexagonal Architecture** (Ports and Adapters)
- **Clean Architecture** (Uncle Bob's pattern)
- **Onion Architecture** (Domain at the center)
- **Bounded Context Architecture**

### **�� Why This Structure?**

This architecture is particularly well-suited for:
- **E-commerce platforms** (like ArtiCurated)
- **Complex business workflows** (order processing, returns)
- **Microservices** (each domain can become a service)
- **Scalable applications** (clear separation of concerns)

Your project structure follows **DDD best practices** and is commonly used in enterprise applications where business logic complexity requires clear domain boundaries and separation of concerns.

```plaintext
   domain/     → Business entities and logic

# 🎨 ArtiCurated - Domain-Driven Design Backend

A robust, scalable backend system for **ArtiCurated**, a boutique online marketplace for high-value artisanal goods. Built using **Domain-Driven Design (DDD)** principles with Spring Boot, this project manages the complete order lifecycle with enterprise-grade architecture.

## 🚀 Key Features

- **🏗️ Domain-Driven Design Architecture** - Clean separation of business domains
- **📦 Order State Management** - Granular tracking from placement to closure
- **💳 Payment Integration** - Secure transaction handling with state machines
- **🔄 Returns & Refunds Workflow** - Multi-step manual approvals with audit trails
- **⚡ Asynchronous Processing** - Background job processing for notifications and updates
- **🔗 Third-Party Integrations** - Payment gateways, shipping providers, email services
- **📊 Audit Logging & History** - Complete transparency for customers and administrators
- **🐳 Docker Ready** - Containerized deployment with PostgreSQL

## 🏛️ Architecture Overview

This project follows **Domain-Driven Design (DDD)** principles with a **Hexagonal Architecture** approach:

```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                    Presentation Layer                       │
│  ┌─────────────┐  ┌─────────────┐  ┌─────────────────────┐ │
│  │   REST API  │  │   Events    │  │   Message Queues    │ │
│  └─────────────┘  └─────────────┘  └─────────────────────┘ │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                    Application Layer                        │
│  ┌─────────────┐  ┌─────────────┐  ┌─────────────────────┐ │
│  │   Services  │  │ State Mgmt  │  │   Event Handlers    │ │
│  └─────────────┘  └─────────────┘  └─────────────────────┘ │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                     Domain Layer                            │
│  ┌─────────────┐  ┌─────────────┐  ┌─────────────────────┐ │
│  │   Entities  │  │   Value     │  │   Domain Services   │ │
│  │             │  │  Objects    │  │                     │ │
│  └─────────────┘  └─────────────┘  └─────────────────────┘ │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                  Infrastructure Layer                       │
│  ┌─────────────┐  ┌─────────────┐  ┌─────────────────────┐ │
│  │ Repositories│  │   External  │  │   Message Brokers   │ │
│  │             │  │   Services  │  │                     │ │
│  └─────────────┘  └─────────────┘  └─────────────────────┘ │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

## 📁 Project Structure

```
ArtiCurated/
├── 📁 src/main/java/com/articurated/
│   ├── 🚀 ArtiCuratedApplication.java          # Main application class
│   │
│   ├── 📁 shared/                              # Cross-cutting concerns
│   │   ├── config/
│   │   │   ├── RabbitMQConfig.java           # Message queue configuration
│   │   │   ├── DatabaseConfig.java          # Connection pooling & JPA
│   │   │   └── SwaggerConfig.java           # API documentation
│   │   ├── exception/
│   │   │   ├── GlobalExceptionHandler.java  # Centralized error handling
│   │   │   └── OrderNotFoundException.java  # Domain-specific exceptions
│   │   └── events/
│   │       ├── GenerateInvoiceEvent.java    # Domain events
│   │       └── ProcessRefundEvent.java      # Event-driven architecture
│   │
│   ├── 📁 order/                              # Order Domain (Bounded Context)
│   │   ├── domain/
│   │   │   ├── Order.java                   # Rich domain entity
│   │   │   ├── OrderState.java              # State enumeration
│   │   │   └── OrderStateHistory.java       # Audit trail
│   │   ├── repository/
│   │   │   ├── OrderRepository.java         # Data access interface
│   │   │   └── OrderStateHistoryRepository.java
│   │   ├── service/
│   │   │   └── OrderService.java            # Business logic orchestration
│   │   ├── controller/
│   │   │   └── OrderController.java         # REST API endpoints
│   │   ├── dto/
│   │   │   ├── CreateOrderRequest.java      # Data transfer objects
│   │   │   └── OrderResponse.java
│   │   └── statemachine/
│   │       └── OrderStateMachineConfig.java # State machine workflow
│   │
│   ├── 📁 returns/                            # Returns Domain (Bounded Context)
│   │   ├── domain/
│   │   │   ├── Return.java                  # Return entity
│   │   │   ├── ReturnState.java             # Return state management
│   │   │   └── ReturnStateHistory.java      # Return audit trail
│   │   ├── service/
│   │   │   └── ReturnService.java           # Return business logic
│   │   ├── controller/
│   │   │   └── ReturnController.java        # Return API endpoints
│   │   └── statemachine/
│   │       └── ReturnStateMachineConfig.java # Return workflow
│   │
│   └── 📁 messaging/                          # Asynchronous Processing
│       ├── producer/
│       │   └── MessageProducer.java         # Queue message production
│       └── consumer/
│           ├── InvoiceMessageConsumer.java  # PDF generation consumer
│           └── RefundMessageConsumer.java   # Payment processing consumer
│
├── 📁 src/main/resources/
│   ├── application.yml                       # Configuration profiles
│   └── db/migration/                         # Database schema migrations
│       ├── V1__Create_orders_schema.sql      # Orders table structure
│       └── V2__Create_returns_schema.sql     # Returns table structure
│
├── 📁 src/test/java/
│   ├── unit/                                 # Unit tests
│   │   └── OrderServiceTest.java            # Service layer testing
│   └── integration/                          # Integration tests
│       └── OrderIntegrationTest.java        # End-to-end testing
│
├── 📁 docker/                                # Containerization
│   ├── Dockerfile                           # Multi-stage application build
│   ├── docker-compose.yml                   # PostgreSQL orchestration
│   └── .dockerignore                        # Build optimization
│
└── 📁 docs/                                  # Documentation
```

## 🛠️ Technology Stack

### **Core Framework**
- **Spring Boot 3.5.4** - Application framework
- **Java 17** - Modern Java features and performance
- **Spring Data JPA** - Data persistence with Hibernate
- **Spring Security** - Authentication and authorization
- **Spring State Machine** - Workflow management

### **Database & Caching**
- **PostgreSQL 15** - Primary database (production)
- **H2 Database** - In-memory database (testing)
- **HikariCP** - High-performance connection pooling

### **Messaging & Integration**
- **Spring Integration** - Enterprise integration patterns
- **RabbitMQ** - Message queuing (planned)
- **Spring Batch** - Background job processing

### **Development & Testing**
- **Maven** - Build and dependency management
- **JUnit 5** - Testing framework
- **Spring Boot Test** - Integration testing
- **Lombok** - Boilerplate code reduction

### **DevOps & Deployment**
- **Docker** - Containerization
- **Docker Compose** - Multi-service orchestration
- **Spring Boot Actuator** - Health monitoring

## 🚀 Quick Start

### **Prerequisites**
- Java 17 or higher
- Maven 3.6+
- Docker & Docker Compose
- PostgreSQL (optional for local development)

### **1. Clone & Build**
```bash
git clone <repository-url>
cd ArtiCurated
./mvnw clean install
```

### **2. Start PostgreSQL (Docker)**
```bash
cd docker
docker-compose up -d postgres
```

### **3. Run Application**
```bash
./mvnw spring-boot:run
```

### **4. Verify Health**
```bash
curl http://localhost:8080/actuator/health
```

## 🔧 Configuration

### **Environment Profiles**
- **default** - PostgreSQL with development settings
- **docker** - Containerized environment
- **test** - H2 in-memory database

### **Key Configuration Properties**
```yaml
spring:
  datasource:
    url: jdbc:postgresql://localhost:5432/articurated
    username: articurated_user
    password: articurated_password
  jpa:
    hibernate:
      ddl-auto: update
    show-sql: true
  security:
    user:
      name: admin
      password: admin123
```

## 📊 API Documentation

### **Available Endpoints**
- **Health Check**: `GET /actuator/health`
- **Application Info**: `GET /actuator/info`
- **Order Management**: `POST /api/orders`
- **Returns Processing**: `POST /api/returns`

### **Authentication**
Basic authentication is enabled by default:
- Username: `admin`
- Password: `admin123`

## 🧪 Testing

### **Run Tests**
```bash
# All tests
./mvnw test

# Skip tests during build
./mvnw package -DskipTests

# Specific test class
./mvnw test -Dtest=OrderServiceTest
```

### **Test Configuration**
- Uses H2 in-memory database
- Disables Spring Batch jobs
- Mock external dependencies

## 🐳 Docker Deployment

### **Build Application Image**
```bash
./mvnw clean package
docker build -t articurated-backend .
```

### **Run with Docker Compose**
```bash
cd docker
docker-compose up -d
```

### **Access Services**
- Application: http://localhost:8080
- PostgreSQL: localhost:5432

- Structured logging with SLF4J
- Configurable log levels per package
- Audit trail for business operations

A robust backend system for **ArtiCurated**, a boutique online marketplace for high-value artisanal goods. Built using **Domain-Driven Design (DDD)** principles with Spring Boot, this project manages the complete order lifecycle with enterprise-grade architecture.

## 🚀 Key Features

- **Domain-Driven Design Architecture** - Clean separation of business domains
- **Order State Management** - Granular tracking from placement to closure
- **Returns & Refunds Workflow** - Multi-step manual approvals with audit trails
- **Asynchronous Processing** - Background job processing for notifications and updates
- **State Machine Workflows** - Order and return lifecycle management
- **Docker Ready** - Containerized deployment with PostgreSQL

For the code present, we get this error:
```
Local variable order is required to be final or effectively final based on its usage
```
How can I resolve this? If you propose a fix, please make it concise.

---

**Cursor**

The error occurs because you're reassigning the `order` variable and then using it in the lambda expression `items.forEach(item -> item.setOrder(order))` on line 64. The lambda requires the variable to be effectively final.

Here's the concise fix - move the `orderRepository.save(order)` call before setting the order reference in items:

```java:src/main/java/com/articurated/order/service/impl/OrderServiceImpl.java
        // Create order
        Order order = Order.builder()
            .orderNumber(generateOrderNumber())
            .customer(customer)
            .amount(amount)
            .items(items)
            .currentState(OrderState.PENDING_PAYMENT)
            .build();
            
        // Save order first to get the ID
        order = orderRepository.save(order);
        
        // Set order reference in items
        items.forEach(item -> item.setOrder(order));
        
        recordStateChange(order, null, OrderState.PENDING_PAYMENT, "Order created");
```

This way, `order` is saved first (getting its ID), then used in the lambda without reassignment, making it effectively final.

```java

        items.forEach(item -> item.setOrder(order));
        
        recordStateChange(order, null, OrderState.PENDING_PAYMENT, "Order created");
```

```java
package com.articurated.order.statemachine;

import com.articurated.order.domain.OrderEvent;
import com.articurated.order.domain.OrderState;
import com.articurated.shared.events.GenerateInvoiceEvent;
import lombok.RequiredArgsConstructor;
import org.springframework.context.ApplicationEventPublisher;
import org.springframework.context.annotation.Bean;
import org.springframework.context.annotation.Configuration;
import org.springframework.statemachine.action.Action;
import org.springframework.statemachine.config.EnableStateMachine;
import org.springframework.statemachine.config.StateMachineBuilder;
import org.springframework.stereotype.Component;

import java.util.EnumSet;

@Configuration
@EnableStateMachine
@RequiredArgsConstructor
public class OrderStateMachineConfig {
    
    private final ApplicationEventPublisher eventPublisher;
    
    @Bean
    public StateMachineBuilder.Builder<OrderState, OrderEvent> stateMachineBuilder() throws Exception {
        StateMachineBuilder.Builder<OrderState, OrderEvent> builder = StateMachineBuilder.builder();
        
        builder.configureStates()
            .withStates()
            .initial(OrderState.PENDING_PAYMENT)
            .states(EnumSet.allOf(OrderState.class));
        
        builder.configureTransitions()
            .withExternal()
                .source(OrderState.PENDING_PAYMENT).target(OrderState.PAID)
                .event(OrderEvent.PAYMENT_RECEIVED)
            .and()
            .withExternal()
                .source(OrderState.PAID).target(OrderState.PROCESSING_IN_WAREHOUSE)
                .event(OrderEvent.START_PROCESSING)
            .and()
            .withExternal()
                .source(OrderState.PROCESSING_IN_WAREHOUSE).target(OrderState.SHIPPED)
                .event(OrderEvent.SHIP_ORDER)
                .action(shipOrderAction())
            .and()
            .withExternal()
                .source(OrderState.SHIPPED).target(OrderState.DELIVERED)
                .event(OrderEvent.DELIVER_ORDER)
            .and()
            .withExternal()
                .source(OrderState.PENDING_PAYMENT).target(OrderState.CANCELLED)
                .event(OrderEvent.CANCEL_ORDER)
            .and()
            .withExternal()
                .source(OrderState.PAID).target(OrderState.CANCELLED)
                .event(OrderEvent.CANCEL_ORDER);
        
        return builder;
    }
    
    @Bean
    public org.springframework.statemachine.StateMachine<OrderState, OrderEvent> stateMachine() throws Exception {
        return stateMachineBuilder().build();
    }
    
    @Component
    @RequiredArgsConstructor
    public static class OrderStateMachineActions {
        
        private final ApplicationEventPublisher eventPublisher;
        
        public Action<OrderState, OrderEvent> shipOrderAction() {
            return context -> {
                Long orderId = (Long) context.getExtendedState().getVariables().get("orderId");
                if (orderId != null) {
                    eventPublisher.publishEvent(new GenerateInvoiceEvent(orderId));
                }
            };
        }
    }
    
    private Action<OrderState, OrderEvent> shipOrderAction() {
        return context -> {
            Long orderId = (Long) context.getExtendedState().getVariables().get("orderId");
            if (orderId != null) {
                eventPublisher.publishEvent(new GenerateInvoiceEvent(orderId));
            }
        };
    }
}

package com.articurated.returns.statemachine;

import com.articurated.returns.domain.ReturnEvent;
import com.articurated.returns.domain.ReturnState;
import com.articurated.shared.events.ProcessRefundEvent;
import lombok.RequiredArgsConstructor;
import org.springframework.context.ApplicationEventPublisher;
import org.springframework.context.annotation.Bean;
import org.springframework.context.annotation.Configuration;
import org.springframework.statemachine.action.Action;
import org.springframework.statemachine.config.EnableStateMachine;
import org.springframework.statemachine.config.StateMachineBuilder;

import java.util.EnumSet;

@Configuration
@EnableStateMachine(name = "returnStateMachine")
@RequiredArgsConstructor
public class ReturnStateMachineConfig {
    
    private final ApplicationEventPublisher eventPublisher;
    
    @Bean
    public StateMachineBuilder.Builder<ReturnState, ReturnEvent> returnStateMachineBuilder() throws Exception {
        StateMachineBuilder.Builder<ReturnState, ReturnEvent> builder = StateMachineBuilder.builder();
        
        builder.configureStates()
            .withStates()
            .initial(ReturnState.REQUESTED)
            .states(EnumSet.allOf(ReturnState.class));
        
        builder.configureTransitions()
            .withExternal()
                .source(ReturnState.REQUESTED).target(ReturnState.APPROVED)
                .event(ReturnEvent.APPROVE)
            .and()
            .withExternal()
                .source(ReturnState.REQUESTED).target(ReturnState.REJECTED)
                .event(ReturnEvent.REJECT)
            .and()
            .withExternal()
                .source(ReturnState.APPROVED).target(ReturnState.IN_TRANSIT)
                .event(ReturnEvent.SHIP_BACK)
            .and()
            .withExternal()
                .source(ReturnState.IN_TRANSIT).target(ReturnState.RECEIVED)
                .event(ReturnEvent.RECEIVE_ITEM)
            .and()
            .withExternal()
                .source(ReturnState.RECEIVED).target(ReturnState.COMPLETED)
                .event(ReturnEvent.PROCESS_REFUND)
                .action(processRefundAction());
        
        return builder;
    }
    
    @Bean
    public org.springframework.statemachine.StateMachine<ReturnState, ReturnEvent> returnStateMachine() throws Exception {
        return returnStateMachineBuilder().build();
    }
    
    private Action<ReturnState, ReturnEvent> processRefundAction() {
        return context -> {
            Long returnId = (Long) context.getExtendedState().getVariables().get("returnId");
            if (returnId != null) {
                eventPublisher.publishEvent(new ProcessRefundEvent(returnId));
            }
        };
    }
}

package com.articurated.order.domain;

import com.articurated.returns.domain.Return;
import jakarta.persistence.*;
import lombok.*;
import org.hibernate.annotations.CreationTimestamp;
import org.hibernate.annotations.UpdateTimestamp;

import java.math.BigDecimal;
import java.time.LocalDateTime;
import java.util.ArrayList;
import java.util.List;

@Entity
@Table(name = "orders")
@Data
@NoArgsConstructor
@AllArgsConstructor
@Builder
public class Order {
    @Id
    @GeneratedValue(strategy = GenerationType.IDENTITY)
    private Long id;
    
    @Column(name = "order_number", nullable = false, unique = true)
    private String orderNumber;
    
    // Customer information (flattened)
    @Column(name = "email", nullable = false)
    private String customerEmail;
    
    @Column(name = "first_name", nullable = false)
    private String customerFirstName;
    
    @Column(name = "last_name", nullable = false)
    private String customerLastName;
    
    // Address information (flattened)
    @Column(name = "street")
    private String street;
    
    @Column(name = "city")
    private String city;
    
    @Column(name = "state")
    private String state;
    
    @Column(name = "zip_code")
    private String zipCode;
    
    @Column(name = "country")
    private String country;
    
    // Amount information (flattened)
    @Column(name = "subtotal", nullable = false, precision = 10, scale = 2)
    private BigDecimal subtotal;
    
    @Column(name = "tax", nullable = false, precision = 10, scale = 2)
    private BigDecimal tax;
    
    @Column(name = "shipping", nullable = false, precision = 10, scale = 2)
    private BigDecimal shipping;
    
    @Column(name = "total", nullable = false, precision = 10, scale = 2)
    private BigDecimal total;
    
    @Enumerated(EnumType.STRING)
    @Column(name = "current_state", nullable = false)
    private OrderState currentState = OrderState.PENDING_PAYMENT;
    
    @CreationTimestamp
    @Column(name = "created_at")
    private LocalDateTime createdAt;
    
    @UpdateTimestamp
    @Column(name = "updated_at")
    private LocalDateTime updatedAt;
    
    @OneToMany(mappedBy = "order", cascade = CascadeType.ALL, fetch = FetchType.LAZY)
    @Builder.Default
    private List<OrderItem> items = new ArrayList<>();
    
    @OneToMany(mappedBy = "order", cascade = CascadeType.ALL, fetch = FetchType.LAZY)
    @Builder.Default
    private List<OrderStateHistory> stateHistory = new ArrayList<>();
    
    @OneToMany(mappedBy = "order", cascade = CascadeType.ALL, fetch = FetchType.LAZY)
    @Builder.Default
    private List<Return> returns = new ArrayList<>();
    
    // Business methods
    public boolean canBeReturned() {
        return this.currentState == OrderState.DELIVERED 
            && this.createdAt.isAfter(LocalDateTime.now().minusDays(30));
    }
    
    public void addStateHistory(OrderState fromState, OrderState toState, String reason) {
        OrderStateHistory history = OrderStateHistory.builder()
            .order(this)
            .fromState(fromState)
            .toState(toState)
            .reason(reason)
            .changedBy("SYSTEM")
            .changedAt(LocalDateTime.now())
            .build();
        this.stateHistory.add(history);
    }
    
    // Helper methods for backward compatibility
    public String getCustomerEmail() {
        return customerEmail;
    }
    
    public String getCustomerFirstName() {
        return customerFirstName;
    }
    
    public String getCustomerLastName() {
        return customerLastName;
    }
    
    public String getFullName() {
        return customerFirstName + " " + customerLastName;
    }
    
    public String getAddress() {
        return street + ", " + city + ", " + state + " " + zipCode + ", " + country;
    }
}
